Hit is ger&aelig-acute;d on gewyrdelícum racum in historical narratives, Homl. Th. i. 58, 10. R&aelig-acute;de him mon ða raca oððe líf ðæra heáhfædera, R. Ben. 66, 17. II. comedy :-- Racu, túnlíc sp&aelig-acute;c comedia, Wrt. Voc. i. 27, 13: 82, 63. III. the art of exposition, rhetoric :-- Swá gedéþ se dreámcræft ðæt se mon biþ dreámere and seó racu déþ ðæt hé biþ reccere sic musica musicos, rhetorica rhetores facit, Bt. 16, 3; Fox 54, 32. IV. an account, reckoning :-- Ð&aelig-acute;r wæs uneten racu unc gem&aelig-acute;ne ; ic onféng ðín sár ðæt ðú móste ges&aelig-acute;lig mínes éðelríces eádig neótan, Exon. Th. 89, 20; Cri. 1460. [O. H. Ger. rahha res, causa, ratio, fabula, circumlocutio.] v. martyr-, riht-, swefnracu ; reccan.
racu, e; f. A rake :-- Hé sceal habban race (cf.. man sceal habban ofnrace, 265, 2), Anglia ix. 263, 7. v. raca, ræce.
racu, e; f. A 'rake' (rake a mountain track across a steep, Cumberland Gloss. e. g. the Lord's rake on Sca-fell), a hollow path, bed of a stream :-- Cf. Andlang bróces ; ðanon . . . on ða ealdan eárace, Cod. Dip. Kmbl. v. 122, 15 ; and see streám-racu. [Ryde doun þis ilk rake, bi &yogh;on rokke syde, Gaw. 2144. Out of the rake of ri&yogh;twisnes renne suld he nevire, Alex. 3384.]
RACU - R&AElig-acute;D
racu, e; f. Rack (?), cloud, storm :-- Ic wille &aelig-acute;hta and ágend eall ácwellan ða beútan beóþ earce bordum ðonne sweart racu (the black clouds that overspread the sky at the Deluge) stígan onginneþ, Cd. Th. 81, 34; Gen. 1355. [Cf. (?) In rede rudede upon rak rises þe sunne, Gaw. 1695. A rak and a royde wynde rose in hor saile, A myst and a merkenes was meruell to se, Destr. Tr. 1984. Or cf. (?) Icel. raki wet, rakr; adj. wet.]
Raculf, Ræculf, Reaculf, Reculf, Raculf-ceaster Reculver in Kent; Regulbium :-- In ðam mynstre ðe is Reaculf nemned, Bd. 5, 8; S. 621, 33. Abbot on Raculfe, Chr. 692; Erl. 43, 13. Reculf, 669; Erl. 34, 26. See Cod. Dip. Kmbl. vi. 324.
rád, e; f. I. riding, going on horseback or in a carriage. v. r&aelig-acute;dwægen :-- Þeáw wæs ðam ylcan biscope ðæt hé ðæt weorc ðæs godspelles má þurh his fóta gange fremede ðonne on his horsa ráde moris erat eidem antistiti opus evangelii magis ambulando per loca quam equitando perficere, Bd. 4, 3; S. 566, 32. Nán mon for ðý ne rít ðe hine rídan lyste, ac rít for ðý ðe hé mid ðære ráde earnaþ sume earnunga. Sume mid ðære ráde earniaþ ðæt hié síen ðý hálran, Bt. 34, 7; Fox 144, 5-8. Ðá wearð his hors gesíclod, and feóll wealwigende geond ða eorþan ... Hé begann ðá tó gereccenne hú him on ráde getímode, Swt. A. S. Rdr. 101, 178. Gif mon on mycelre ráde oððe on miclum gangum weorðe geteorad, Lchdm. i. 76, 4. Ðæt man funde &aelig-acute;nne man tó ráde oððe tó gange, L. Ath. v. 4; Th. i. 232, 15. Rynestrong on ráde, Exon. Th. 400, 9; Rä. 20, 7. I a. going in a ship :-- Sió cwén bebeád áras fýsan tó ráde, sceoldon Rómwarena ofer heánne holm hláford sécean, Elen. Kmbl. 1960 ; El. 982. II. an expedition on horseback; in a hostile sense a raid :-- Ðonne rídan ða yldestan men tó ... and nimon eall ðæt hé áge, and fó se cyning tó healfum, tó healfum ða men ðe on ðære ráde beón, L. Ath. i. 20; Th. i. 210, 7. Gif áðor oððe m&aelig-acute;g oððe fremde ða ráde forsace, L. C. S. 25; Th. i. 390, 24. Cyninges þegnas oft ráde onridon, Chr. 871; Erl. 76, 11. III. a road; in the compounds brim-, hran-, hweogol-, segl-, streám-, swan-, wíg-rád. IV. the name of the Runic R. v. Exon. Th. 440, 10; Rä. 59, 25. See also next word. [Icel. reið riding; a raid.] v. mid-, on-, setl-, swegl-, þunor-rád.
rád, e; f. Furniture (of a house), harness (of a horse) :-- Rád byþ on recyde rinca gehwylcum séfte and swíðhwæt ðam ðe sitteþ onufan meare mægenheardum ofer mílpaþas in the house is for each man furniture soft, and (the furniture for the horse, the harness) very strong for him that sits on the stout steed, traversing the roads, Runic pm. Kmbl. 349, 11; Rún. 5. [Cf. Icel. reiða implements, outfit; reiði; n. harness; reiði; m. tackle, harness.] v. brand-rád, ge-r&aelig-acute;de, r&aelig-acute;de-sceamol.
rád, L. Wih. 50; Th. i. 38, 21. v. r&aelig-acute;d.
-rád. v. ge-, sam-rád.
rád-cniht, es; m. A title equivalent to that of sixhynde man :-- Si autem talis occiditur qualem supra nominavimus rádcniht, et quidam Angli. vocant sixhændeman, Text. Roff. p. 38. In dome hominis, quem Angli vocant rádcniht, alii veto sexhendeman, Schmid. A. S. Gesetz. 93, note 6.
rád-here, es. v. r&aelig-acute;de-here.
rád-hors, es; n. A horse for riding, a saddle-horse :-- Man sceal J&aelig-acute;tan hine rídan on ðæs cyninges rádhorse, Anglia ix. 35, 235. [Wick. rood-hors a horse for a chariot : O. H. Ger. reit-hros currilis equus.]
-rádian, rador, v. ge-rádian, rodor.
radre glosses bovistra, Wrt. Voc. ii. 11, 26 : 102, 10.
rád-stefn, e; f. A term of service performed by a mounted person (?) :-- Gif þegen geþeáh ðæt hé þénode cyning, and his rádstefne rád on his híréde, L. R. 3 ; Th. i. 190, 19. v. stefn.
rád-wægen. v. r&aelig-acute;d-wægen.
rád-wérig; adj. Weary with riding or journeying, Exon. Th. 401, 19; Rä. 21, 14.
r&aelig-acute;can; p. r&aelig-acute;hte. I. intrans. To reach, extend, stretch forth :-- Ic wíde r&aelig-acute;ce ofer engla eard, Exon. Th. 482, 26; Rä. 67, 7. Yldo r&aelig-acute;ceþ wíde, Salm. Kmbl. 588; Sal. 294. Heó r&aelig-acute;hte mid handum tó heofoncyninge, Cd. Th. 292, 7; Sat. 437 : Beo. Th. 1499; B. 747. R&aelig-acute;hton wíde geond werþeóda wróhtes telgan, Cd. Th. 61, 1; Gen. 990. Ne hé sóðfæste l&aelig-acute;teþ ðæt hí tó unrihte willen handum r&aelig-acute;cean ut non extendan justi ad iniquitatem manus suas, Ps. Th. 124, 4. II. trans. To reach, hold forth, offer, present :-- Ic r&aelig-acute;ce porrigo vel porgo, Ælfc. Gr. 28, 5; Som. 31, 46. Hé ys se ðe ic r&aelig-acute;ce (porrexero) hláf, Jn. Skt. 13, 26. For hwon ne r&aelig-acute;cst (porrigis) ðú ús ðone hwítan hláf ? Bd. 2, 5; S. 507, 14. R&aelig-acute;cþ (porrigit) hé him scorpionem? Lk. Skt. 11, 12. Ð&aelig-acute;r (in hell) hý leomu r&aelig-acute;caþ (stretch forth) tó bindenne, Exon. Th. 99, 8; Cri. 1621. Eall ða weoruldgód hé gefeónde þearfum r&aelig-acute;hte and sealde cuncta pauperibus erogare gaudebat, Bd. 3, 5; S. 526, 26. Hé hláf bræc and him r&aelig-acute;hte, Lk. Skt. 24, 30. Se óðer r&aelig-acute;hte forþ (protulit) his hand, Gen. 38, 28. Heó r&aelig-acute;hte hire handa ,him tó, Th. Ap. 27, 1 : Past. 36, 1; Swt. 247, 21. Ðara ánra ðe for neóde him þénunge æt ðæs mynstres ingange r&aelig-acute;can scylon, R. Ben. 139, 11. Se gebúr sceal erian healfne æcer and r&aelig-acute;can (cf. on bærene gebringan, Chart. Th. 145, 1) ðæt s&aelig-acute;d on hláfordes berne, Cod. Dip. Kmbl. iii. 450, 35. [O. Frs. réka : O. H. Ger, reihhen.] v. á-, ge-, mis-r&aelig-acute;can.
ræcc, es; m. A dog that hunts by scent :-- Ræcc bruccus, Wrt. Voc. i. 288, 29. [Rache a dog that discovers and pursues his prey by the scent, Jamieson. Rihht alls an hunnte takeþþ der wiþþ hise &yogh;3æpe racchess, Orm. 13505. See other passages in Halliwell's Dict. Icel. rakki a dog.]
ræce, an; f. A rake :-- Raece rastrum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 98, 28. v. raca.
ræced, reced, es; m. n. A house, hall, palace :-- Reced sélesta (Hrothgar's hall), Beo. Th. 828; B. 412 : 1545; B. 770. Ræced, 3603; B. 1799. Wið ðæs recedes weal, 658; B. 326 : 1452; B. 724. His (Lot) recedes hleów, Cd. Th. 147, 18; Gen. 1441. Se beorn (Noah) reste on recede, 95. 25; Gen. 1584. In ræcede, Exon. Th. 314, 21; Mód. 17 : 413, 11; Rä. 32, 3. Recyde, Runic pm. Kmbl. 340, 11; Rún. 5. Ic seah r&aelig-acute;plingas in ræced fergan, Exon. Th. 435, 2; Rä. 53, 1. Con hé sídne ræced fæste gefégan, 296, 7; Crä. 47. In ðæt dimme ræced (a prison), Andr. Kmbl. 2618; An. 1310. Reced, Beo. Th. 2479; B. 1237. Hwearf geond ðæt síde reced, 3966; B. 1981. Ðæt (Hrothgar's hall) wæs forem&aelig-acute;rost receda, 625; B. 310. Receda wuldor, Salomones templ, Cd. Th. 219, 23; Dan. 59. Hié on Sodoman wlítan meahton, gesáwon ofer since salo hlifian, reced ofer reádum golde, 145, 11; Gen. 2404. Ræced, Exon. Th. 381, 4; Rä. 2, 6. [O. Sax. rakud used of the Temple.] v. burg-, deáþ-, eorþ-, gim-, heáh-, heal-, hlín-, horn-, sund-, wín-ræced, and next word.
ræced-líc; adj. Pertaining to a palace, palatine :-- Ræcedlíce palatina, Wrt. Voc. ii. 116, 7.
r&aelig-acute;cing, e; f. Reaching, holding out, offering, presenting, extending :-- Hláfes mið r&aelig-acute;cing panis porrectione, Jn. Skt. p. 7, 3. Mið rácing honda extensione manuum, 8, 11.
r&aelig-acute;d, es; m. I. counsel, advice :-- R&aelig-acute;d consilium, Wrt. Voc. i. 73, 23. Ðæt hit n&aelig-acute;fre næs náðer ne his gewile, ne his geweald, ne his r&aelig-acute;d, L. C. S. 76; Th. i. 418, 12. Is micel þearf ðisse þeóde helpes and r&aelig-acute;des, Wulfst. 243, 5 : Elen. Kmbl. 1103; El. 553. Sum woruldwita wæs swýðe wís on r&aelig-acute;de Acitofel geháten ... Ðá wæs se Acitofel mid Absalone on r&aelig-acute;de and r&aelig-acute;dde him hú hé mihte beswícan his fæder, Homl. Skt. i. 19, 196-203. Ðíne heortan tó r&aelig-acute;de gecyr turn thine heart to listen to good advice, Blickl. Homl. 113, 27. On ðone Drihten næs ic æt r&aelig-acute;de ne æt d&aelig-acute;de, ð&aelig-acute;r man mid unrihte N. orf ætferede, L. O. 3; Th. i. 178, 17. Gyf mon ðone hláford teó ðæt hé (the accused person) be his r&aelig-acute;de út hleópe, L. Eth. i. 1; Th. i. 282, 5, 12. Gif þeów ete his sylfes r&aelig-acute;de if a slave eat flesh during a fast of his own accord (i. e. when his master does not give the meat. v. the paragraph which precedes), L. Wih. 15; Th. i. 40, 11. Ráde, 10; Th. i. 38, 21. Ic ðá féng on mínne ágenne réd, Chart. Th. 322, 10. Gehýr míne word and mínne r&aelig-acute;d, Ex. 18, 19. Ðæt hí ðæs cynges r&aelig-acute;d hæfdon and his fultum and ealra witena, Chr. 1048; Erl. 178, 22. R&aelig-acute;d gel&aelig-acute;ran to give good advice (cf. sellan hálwende geþeahte, Bd. 1, 1; S. 474, 14), pref. ; Erl. 3, 10. R&aelig-acute;d sóhtan consulunt, Wrt. Voc. ii. 21, 3. II. counsel, prudence, intelligence :-- Nis nán wisdóm ne nán r&aelig-acute;d náht ongeán God, Homl. Th. i. 82, 14. Ongeán ðam wíslícan r&aelig-acute;de ðe of Godes ágenre gyfe cymþ, se wiðerr&aelig-acute;da deófol s&aelig-acute;wþ réceleásnesse, Wulfst. 53, 6. Se man ána hæfþ gesceád and r&aelig-acute;d and andgit, Homl. Skt. i. 1, 99. III. counsel, course of action that results from deliberation, plan, a resolution taken after deliberation, ordinance, decree :-- Sý ðes r&aelig-acute;d gem&aelig-acute;ne eallum leódscipe, L. Edg. S. 2; Th. i. 272, 33. Se r&aelig-acute;d wæs &aelig-acute;fre on his r&aelig-acute;dfæstum geþance, ðæt hé wircan wolde ða wunderlícan gesceafta, Ælfc. T. Grn. 2, 4. Hé him tó r&aelig-acute;de genom ðæt ... cui rei consilium utile ratus est, ut ... Ors. 4, 5; Swt. 166, 27. Hé Rómánum tó r&aelig-acute;de gel&aelig-acute;rde, ðæt hié fóren on Hannibales land, 4, 10; Swt. 200, 1. On ðisum r&aelig-acute;de (the conspiracy against William Rufus) wæs Oda, Chr. 1087; Erl. 224, 5. Ðæne r&aelig-acute;d (paying the Danes) ger&aelig-acute;dde Síríc, 991; Erl. 131, 19. R&aelig-acute;d geþencean, Cd. Th. 19, 4; Gen. 286 : 35, 28; Gen. 561. R&aelig-acute;d áhicgan, 122, 24; Gen. 2031 : 131, 24; Gen. 2181. R&aelig-acute;das consulta, Wrt. Voc. ii. 19, 54 : consulta, consilia, 133, 80 : Hpt. Gl. 504. 75 : decreta, judicia, edicta, 433. 19. Gel&aelig-acute;rdan biscepas swelce níwe r&aelig-acute;das swelce hié fol oft &aelig-acute;r ealde gedydan, Ors. 4, 7; Swt. 184, 2. Manna wísdóm and heore r&aelig-acute;das syndon náhtlíce ongeán Godes geþeaht, Chr. 979; Erl. 129, 26. IV. what is advisable, benefit, advantage :-- R&aelig-acute;d opere pretium, Wrt. Voc. ii. 64, 31. R&aelig-acute;d biþ gif hé nimþ mealwan it will be worth his while to take mallow, Lchdm. ii. 238, 13. Biþ nú micel r&aelig-acute;d, ðæt hé him gebycge ðæt éce líf, Homl. Skt. i. 12, 122. Ðonne biþ hire r&aelig-acute;d ðæt frýnd ða forword habban, L. Edm. B. 7; Th. i. 256, 2. Ðæt heó ús sý þingere ondweardes r&aelig-acute;des and éces wuldres that she be for us an advocate for present profit and eternal glory, Blickl. Homl. 159, 34. Hí him tó r&aelig-acute;de and tó frófre fundon aliquid commodi adlaturum putabant, Bd. 1, 12; S. 481, 7 : 2, 5; S. 507, 31. Ðis him tó r&aelig-acute;de gecuron hoc esse tutius decernebant, 1, 23; S. 485, 34. Tó r&aelig-acute;de Angelcynne to the advantage of the English, 2, 1; S. 501, 39 : Blickl. Homl. 199, 30 : 205, 12. Tó h&aelig-acute;le and tó r&aelig-acute;de, 227, 4. Ðam þeódscype tó langsuman r&aelig-acute;de to the lasting benefit of the nation, L. I. P. 4; Th. ii. 308, 6. Eów sylfum tó r&aelig-acute;de, Ælfc. T. Grn. 12, 2. R&aelig-acute;d áredian to determine what is advisable, L. Eth. vi. 40; Th. i. 324, 28. Ða ðe heora sylfra r&aelig-acute;d forl&aelig-acute;taþ those who forsake their own advantage, Blickl. Homl. 103, 16. R&aelig-acute;da fyrmest ðæt manna gehwylc ofer ealle óðre þinc &aelig-acute;nne God lufige, L. I. P. 24; Th. ii. 338, 1. V. a council :-- Hé eode tó ðæra Judéiscra r&aelig-acute;de and befrán, hwæt hí him feós geúðon, Homl. Th. ii. 242, 16. Se cyng beád heom ðæt hí cómon mid. xii. mannum intó ðæs cynges r&aelig-acute;de, Chr. 1048; Erl. 180, 11. VI. as a part of proper names, generally under the form réd (red ?). For a list of such names v. Txts, 603 sqq., and for similar O. H. Ger. names v. Grff. ii. 463. [O. Sax. rád : O. Frs. réd : O. H. Ger. rát : Icel. ráð.] v. feorh-, folc-, mis-, un-r&aelig-acute;d.
R&AElig-acute;D[E] - R&AElig-acute;DELS
r&aelig-acute;d[e] in composition of adjectives, v. án-, fæst-, heard-, hwæt-, læt-, wiðer-r&aelig-acute;d[e].
r&aelig-acute;dan. Two verbs originally distinct seem to coalesce under this form, the strong r&aelig-acute;dan; p. reórd, réd; pp. r&aelig-acute;den : Goth. ga-rédan : O. Sax. rádan; p. réd, ried : O. Frs. réda; p. réd : O. H. Ger. rátan; p. riet, riat : Icel. ráða; p. réð, and the weak r&aelig-acute;dan; p. r&aelig-acute;dde : Goth. ga-raidjan : O. H. Ger. ant-reitjan ordinare : Icel. g-reiða. The strong forms are rare. I. to counsel, give advice :-- Ic r&aelig-acute;de ðé consulo tibi, Wrt. Voc. i. 49, 37. Girwan Godes tempel, swá hire gásta weard reórd, Elen. Kmbl. 2043; El. 1023. Hé rád and r&aelig-acute;dde, rincum t&aelig-acute;hte hú hí sceoldon standan, Byrht. Th. 132, 18; By. 18. Ðæt folc eall hrýmde, swá swá Josue him r&aelig-acute;dde, Jos. 6, 5 (20, Grn.). R&aelig-acute;dende consulentes, consilium dantes, Hpt. Gl. 491, 20. II. to ask advice, consult a person :-- Ic fríne vel ic r&aelig-acute;de consulo, i. inquiro (cf. ic fríne ðé consulo te, i. 49, 38), Wrt. Voc. ii. 133, 79. II a. to consult, deliberate, take counsel upon a matter (acc.) with (wið) a person :-- Justinus r&aelig-acute;dde wið ða cristenan, hwæne hí tó bisceope ceósan wolde, Homl. Th. i. 434, 28. Wið ðone r&aelig-acute;dde Chromatius, and be his r&aelig-acute;de underféng ealle ða cristenan, Homl. Skt. i. 5, 323. Him þúhte and ð&aelig-acute;m ðé hé hit wið r&aelig-acute;dde, L. Ath. v. 12; Th. i. 240, 27. Hí gamenlíce r&aelig-acute;ddon callide cogitantes, Jos. 9, 4. Ðá gesomnedon hí gemót and þeahtedon and r&aelig-acute;ddon hwæt him tó dónne w&aelig-acute;re initum est consilium quid agendum, Bd. 1, 14; S. 482, 36. Ðá rédon (r&aelig-acute;ddan, MSS. C.) hí him betweónum consultatione habita, Ors. 1, 14; Swt. 56, 20. Ðá ongunnon ða Phariséi r&aelig-acute;dan consilium inierunt, Mt. Kmbl. 22, 15. Bisceopum gebyreþ ðæt symle mid heom wunian wel geþungene witan, ðæt hí wið r&aelig-acute;dan mágan, L. I. P. 10 ; Th. ii. 316, 23. Man r&aelig-acute;dan sceolde hú man ðisne eard werian sceolde, Chr. l010; Erl.144, 7. II b. to debate, speak in council (or (?) to read. v. VI b) :-- Rádaþ (r&aelig-acute;daþ) ł maðeliaþ concionantur, sermocinantur, loquuntur, Hpt. Gl. 461, 1. R&aelig-acute;dende ł wordiende concionandi, loquentes, 461, 35. II c. to deliberate for the good of any one, look to, provide for :-- Míne sáwle r&aelig-acute;d on écnysse animae meae in aeternum consules, L. Ecg. P. iv. 67; Th. ii. 228, 3. R&aelig-acute;dende consulens, i. consilium tenens, providens, Wrt. Voc. ii. 133, 77. R&aelig-acute;dende consulentes, succurrentes, Hpt. Gl. 491, 20. III. to resolve after deliberation, to determine, decide :-- Ðæt folc r&aelig-acute;dde be him ðæt hí woldon hine áhebban tó cyninge ... Ðá ðá Crist ongeat ðæs folces willan, Homl. Th. i. 162, 3-6. Acðeáh man hwæt r&aelig-acute;dde, ðæt ne stód furðon &aelig-acute;nne mónaþ, Chr. 1010; Erl. 144, 9. Hí r&aelig-acute;ddon ðæt hí woldon ðone cyng gesettan út of Englalandes cynedóme, 1075; Erl. 213, 10. Hí ealle ánmódlíce r&aelig-acute;ddon ðæt ealle his gesetnyssa áýdlode w&aelig-acute;ron, Homl. Th. i. 60, 4. R&aelig-acute;dan decernere, Wrt. Voc. ii. 27, 67. III a. r&aelig-acute;dan on (cf. Icel. ráða á einn to attack one) to proceed against, take action against a person :-- Wæs ðam eorle Godwine and his sunan gecýdd, ðæt se cyng and ða menn ðe mid him w&aelig-acute;ron woldon r&aelig-acute;don on hí, Chr. 1048; Erl. 178, 30. IV. to rule, govern, direct (with dat. or inst.) :-- Ðú ðe Israéla &aelig-acute;ðelum cynne reccest and r&aelig-acute;dest qui regis Israel, Ps. Th. 79,1. Hé r&aelig-acute;t ús and recþ ipse reget nos, 47, 12. Drihten mé r&aelig-acute;t (regit), 22, 1. God ðe r&aelig-acute;t and gewissaþ eallum gesceaftum, Chart. Th. 239, 34. Hé reht anð r&aelig-acute;t eallum gesceaftum, swá swá gód steóra ánum scipe, Bt. 35, 3; Fox 158, 25. God ðe him stiórde and racode and r&aelig-acute;dde, 34,12; Fox 154, 6. Ðætte God r&aelig-acute;dde and weólde ealles middaneardes, 35, 2; Fox 156, 31. Ðæt hé (the abbot) sceal r&aelig-acute;dan and racian óðra manna sáulum, R. Ben. 14, 6. Hwá meahte iéð monnum r&aelig-acute;dan bútan scylde quis principari hominibus tam sine culpa potuisset ? Past. 3, 1; Swt. 33, 16. Ðam ðe hié (the Church) wel ofer m&aelig-acute;ge and hiere wel r&aelig-acute;dan cunne ei qui hanc bene regere praevalet, 5, 2; Swt. 45, 1. Ic mæg r&aelig-acute;dan on ðís ríce, Cd. Th. 19, l0; Gen. 289. Ða ðe ðý ríce r&aelig-acute;dan sceoldon, 259, 4; Dan. 686. Wolde dóm Godes d&aelig-acute;dum r&aelig-acute;dan gumena gehwylcum the decree of God would govern the deeds of every man, Beo. Th. 5709; B. 2858. V. to have the disposal of, have possession of :-- Ðone máððum ðe ðú mid rihte r&aelig-acute;dan sceoldest, 4119; B. 2056. Ðenden hié ðý ríce r&aelig-acute;dan móston, Cd. Th. 216, 18; Dan. 8. Bútan hý ðý reáfe r&aelig-acute;dan mótan, Exon. Th. 110, 6; Gú. 103. VI. to read (a) as in to read a riddle, to explain; conjicere :-- Ic r&aelig-acute;de swefn conicio, Ælfc. Gr. 28, 6; Som. 32, 40. Módor ne r&aelig-acute;doþ (-aþ, MS.) ðonne heó magan cenneþ, hú him weorðe geond woruld sceapen a mother cannot read a boy's fate at his birth, Salm. Kmbl. 741; Sal. 370. R&aelig-acute;de se ðe wille hú wunda cw&aelig-acute;den, Exon. Th. 441, 11; Rä. 60, 16. R&aelig-acute;d hwæt ic m&aelig-acute;ne, 479, 18; Rä. 62, 9. Ðá ongan hé mid gleáwe móde r&aelig-acute;dan coepit sagaci animo conjicere, Bd. 3, 10; S. 534, 21, MS. B. (b) to read a book; legere :-- Ic r&aelig-acute;de lego, ðú r&aelig-acute;tst legis, Ælfc. Gr. 22; Som. 24, 1. R&aelig-acute;tt legit, 44; Som. 45, 49. On hwylcum dæge man r&aelig-acute;t .ix. kl. apr. swá fela beóþ concurrentes ... gif man r&aelig-acute;t ðæne datu-rum on Sunnandæg ðænne byþ án, Anglia viii. 302, 19-20. Se ðe r&aelig-acute;t (r&aelig-acute;dæ, Rush.), Mt. Kmbl. 24, 15. Hé r&aelig-acute;dde his bóc ðam folce, Ex. 24, 7. Hé him gebæd and his béc r&aelig-acute;dde, Bd. 4, 3; S. 567, 4. Ne r&aelig-acute;dde gé (gé hreórdeþ, Rush.) hwæt Dauid dyde, Mt. Kmbl. 12, 3. Ne r&aelig-acute;dde gé (gé ne reórdade, Rush.), 19, 4. R&aelig-acute;ddon (reórdadun, Rush.), 21, 16. R&aelig-acute;dde (reórdun, Rush.), 21, 42. Mé lyst r&aelig-acute;dan lecturio, Ælfc. Gr. 34; Som. 37, 56. Réða to read, Mt. Kmbl. p. 1, 8. Hé árás tó rédanne, Lk. Skt. Rush. Lind. 4, 16 : Rtl. 195, 16. Hé mé sealde bóc tó r&aelig-acute;danne, Bd. 5, 13; S. 632, 37. Ðæt gewrit wæs r&aelig-acute;ded beforan ðam cyninge, 5, 21; S. 643, 11. Ðá ðæt godspel r&aelig-acute;dd wæs, Blickl. Homl. 161, 9. Wé gehýrdon ðá ðá Esaias se wítga r&aelig-acute;den wæs, 167, 28. VII. to prepare (?) :-- Hé sceal &aelig-acute;lcre wucan erian .i. æcer and r&aelig-acute;dan sylf ðæt s&aelig-acute;d on hlafordes berne, L. R. S. 4; Th. i. 434, 15. (Cf. last passage under r&aelig-acute;can.) v. á-, be-, for-, ge-, mis-, ofer-r&aelig-acute;dan.
r&aelig-acute;d-bana, an; m. One who contrives a person's death, but is not the actual perpetrator :-- Gif man secge ðæt hé w&aelig-acute;re d&aelig-acute;dbana oððe r&aelig-acute;dbana if he be said to be the actual perpetrator of homicide, or the deviser of it, L. Eth. ix. 23; Th. i. 344, 26. Cf. Qui ad occidendum aliquem innoxium redbana vel dedbana fuerit, L. H. I. 85, 3; Th. i. 592, 13. [Icel. ráð-bani : see also bana-ráð the planning a person's death; ráða einum bana to plot a person's death. v. Grmm. R. A. 626.]
r&aelig-acute;d-bora, an; m. A counsellor; also translates consul :-- R&aelig-acute;dbora consiliarius, Wrt. Voc. i. 73, 22. Hé (the Messiah) biþ geháten wundorlíc, r&aelig-acute;dbora, strang God, Homl. Th. ii. 16, 7 : Dóm. L. 42, 38. Aðelwold ðe is mín r&aelig-acute;dbora a secretis noster Athelwoldus, Chart. Th. 241, 27 : Beo. Th. 2655; B. 1325. God næfþ n&aelig-acute;nne r&aelig-acute;dboran, Ælfc. T. Grn. 24, 24. Hí hæfdon him Consulas ðæt wé cweðaþ R&aelig-acute;dboran, Jud. Thw. p. 161, 22. Seó ger&aelig-acute;dnes ðe Angelcynnes witan and Wealhþeóde r&aelig-acute;dboran gesetton, L. O. D. tit. ; Th. i. 352, 2. R&aelig-acute;dboran jurisperiti, Wrt. Voc. ii. 46, 41. Rédboran, 112, 13. R&aelig-acute;dborena juris peritorum, Hpt. Gl. 524, 68. Cf. r&aelig-acute;d-gifa.
r&aelig-acute;de (?), an; f. A reading, lesson :-- Ðiós rédo haec lectio, Lk. Skt. p. 11, 16. Ðió rédo quae lectio, 11, 5. Rédes lectionis, Mt. Kmbl. p. 10, 16. Ðara réda lectionum, 13, 13. Tó réde ad lectionem, Rtl. 126, 1. Hálige r&aelig-acute;dan (r&aelig-acute;dincge, MS. T.) hé sceal lustlíce gehýran, R. Ben. 18, 9.
-r&aelig-acute;de. v. ge-r&aelig-acute;de; n.
r&aelig-acute;de; adj. Ready, prompt :-- On hwan mæg se iunga on gódne weg riht[r]an ne (ðe ?) r&aelig-acute;dran r&aelig-acute;d gemittan ðonne hé ðíne wísan word gehealde in quo corrigit junior viam sitam? in custodiendo sermones tuos, Ps. Th. 118, 9. R&aelig-acute;dan (?) biionges exercitationis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 29, 59. v. ge-r&aelig-acute;de, r&aelig-acute;de-gafol, r&aelig-acute;de-sceamol, r&aelig-acute;dness.
r&aelig-acute;de; adj. Mounted :-- R&aelig-acute;dum here equitatu, Hpt. Gl. 525, 25. v. r&aelig-acute;de-cempa, -here, -mann.
r&aelig-acute;de-cempa, an; m. A mounted soldier :-- R&aelig-acute;dewíga vel [r&aelig-acute;de] -cempa equester, qui equitat, Wrt. Voc. ii. 143, 66. v. r&aelig-acute;de-here.
r&aelig-acute;de-gafol, es; n. Rent that can be paid all at once, as opposed to rent that is discharged by service rendered, and consequently takes time for its payment :-- Gif mon geþingaþ gyrde landes oððe máre tó r&aelig-acute;degafole and geereþ gif se hláford him wile ðæt land ár&aelig-acute;ran tó weorce and tó gafole ne þearf hé him onfón gif hé him nán botl ne selþ if a man takes a yard of land or more at a fixed rent and ploughs it, if the lord wants to get service as well as rent, the tenant need not take the land, if the lord does not give him a dwelling, L. In. 67; Th. i. 146, 3. [Cf. Icel. reiðu-penningar ready money.]
r&aelig-acute;de-here, es; m. A mounted force, cavalry :-- R&aelig-acute;dehere cerethi, Wrt. Voc. ii. 15, 76 : cerethei, 130, 15. Of rádehere equitatu, Hpt. Gl. 525, 25. Alexandres næs ná má geslægen ðonne hundtwelftig on ðæm r&aelig-acute;dehere in exercitu Alexandri centum et viginti equites defuere, Ors. 3, 9; Swt. 124, 21. &AElig-acute;gðer ge an gangehere ge on r&aelig-acute;dehere (rád-, MS. C.), 4, 1; Swt. 154, 24. Earnulf gefeaht wið ðæm r&aelig-acute;dehere (ráde-, MS. B.: rád-, MS. D.), Chr. 891; Erl. 88, 2.
r&aelig-acute;delle. v. next word.
r&aelig-acute;dels, es; m.: e; f.: r&aelig-acute;delse, r&aelig-acute;delle (?), an; f. I. counsel, consideration :-- Seó rédelse and ðæt geþeaht úrra feónda geteorode, Ps. Th. 9, 6. II. debate, speech in council (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, II b) :-- R&aelig-acute;delse concionis, locutionis, Hpt. Gl. 461, 4. III. conjecture, imagination, interpretation (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, VI a) :-- R&aelig-acute;swung vel r&aelig-acute;dels conjecture, i. opinatio, estimatio, interpretatio, Wrt. Voc. ii. 133, 53. Ðeáh se leása wéna and sió r&aelig-acute;delse ðara dysigena monna tiohhie ðæt se anweald síe ðæt héhste gód (hominum fallax opinio), Bt. 27, 3; Fox 98, 32. Eall ðis ðú gerehtest tó sóðe swíðe gesceádwíslíce búton &aelig-acute;lcre leásre r&aelig-acute;delsan haec nullis extrinsecus sumtis, sed altero ex altero fidem trahente, insitis domesticisque probationibus explicabas, 35, 5; Fox 164, 31. Hr&aelig-acute;delse conjectura, argumentatione, Hpt. Gl. 443, 19. Of r&aelig-acute;delse conjectura, 460, 11. III a. the imaginative faculty :-- Hé (man) hine ongit þurh his r&aelig-acute;delsan (imaginatio) synderlíce, þurh his gesceádwísnesse (ratio) synderlíce, Bt. 41, 5; Fox 252, 19. IV. a dark saying, enigma, riddle :-- R&aelig-acute;dels aenigma, Ælfc. Gr. 9, 1; Som. 8, 23. Hé ásette r&aelig-acute;dels ðus cweðende : Swá hwilc man swá mínne r&aelig-acute;dels riht ár&aelig-acute;de onfó se mýnre dohtor tó wífe, and se ðe hine misr&aelig-acute;de, sý hé beheáfdod, Ap. Th. 3, 8-11. The riddle is given on p.4. Ða clamme ðe ða r&aelig-acute;dellan (r&aelig-acute;delsan ?) wið rýnemenn heáld, Exon. Th. 423, 31; Rä. 43, 13. Ic sprece tó him openlíce næs þurh rédelsas (per aenigmata; dark speeches, A. V.), Num. 12, 8. [Wick. redels : Piers P. redel, ridel : Prompt. Parv. rydyl or probleme enigma : M. H. Ger. rátsal : M. L. Ger. rédelse.] v. r&aelig-acute;sele.
R&AElig-acute;DELSE - R&AElig-acute;D-LEÁS
r&aelig-acute;delse. v. preceding word.
r&aelig-acute;de-mann, es; m. A horseman :-- Náwðer ne ðam horse ne ðæm r&aelig-acute;demen ne wyrð geborgen of his ágnum cræfte, Ps. Th. 32, 15. [Icel. reið-maðr. ]
r&aelig-acute;den[n], e; f. I. a condition, stipulation :-- R&aelig-acute;den conditio, Hpt. Gl. 436, 1. Rédin condicio, Wrt. Voc. i. 288, 44 : ii. 17, 10. &AElig-acute;lc gebúr sylle .vi. hláfas ðam inswáne ðonne hé his heorde tó mæstene drífe, on ðam sylfum lande ðe ðeós r&aelig-acute;den on stænt, L. R. S. 4; Th. i. 434, 22. R&aelig-acute;denne condicione, Wrt. Voc. ii. 104, 59. Ðan (on ða ?) r&aelig-acute;denne ea conditione, Hpt. Gl. 492, 8. On ða r&aelig-acute;denne ðe hé him gá tó honda, L. In. 62; Th. i. 142, 3. Ðú bist Godes bearn þurh ða r&aelig-acute;denne ðæt ðú ðínne feónd lufige, Homl. Th. i. 56, 7. Raedinnae condiciones, Ep. GI. 7 f, 13. II. rule, direction (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, IV) :-- Hæfdon sume mid áþum gefæstnod ðæt hié on hire r&aelig-acute;denne (r&aelig-acute;dinge, 193, col. a) beón woldan would be under her rule, Chr. 918; Th. i. 192, 12. III. a reckoning, estimating :-- Raedinne taxatione, Wrt. Voc. ii. 122, 1. The word occurs as the second part of many nouns, when its force is much the same as that of the suffixes -ship, -hood, -red, denoting a state, condition. v. bed-, bróðor-, burh-, camp-, feónd-, folc-, freónd-, gafol-, gebed-, gecwid-, gefér-, heord-, híw-, hús-, land-, m&aelig-acute;g-, mann-, meodo-, nám-, teón-, þing-, treów-, un-, weorc-, wíg-, woroldr&aelig-acute;den[n].
r&aelig-acute;dend, es; m. A ruler, one who possesses control over anything (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, IV) :-- Rodera r&aelig-acute;dend the Deity, Chr. 975 ; Erl. 126, 17 : Beo. Th. 3114; B. 1555 : Andr. Kmbl. 1253; An. 627. Dreáma r&aelig-acute;dend, Exon. Th. 358, 34; Pa. 55. [O. Sax. r&aelig-acute;dand (Christ).] v. mago-, sele-r&aelig-acute;dend.
r&aelig-acute;dend-líc; adj. Pertaining to a decree or statute (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, III) :-- Ð&aelig-acute;m r&aelig-acute;dendlícum decretalibus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 26, 45.
r&aelig-acute;den-gewrit, es; n. A writing containing a condition or stipulation, a written agreement, a note of hand :-- Ic him sealde úre ágen r&aelig-acute;dengewrit, ðæt w&aelig-acute;re him tó ðam geráde ðæt land tó l&aelig-acute;ten, ðe mon &aelig-acute;lce gére gesylle fífténe scillingas cl&aelig-acute;nes feós ðam bisceope, Chart. Th. 168, 12. R&aelig-acute;dinggewrit (r&aelig-acute;den- ?) cirographum, Wrt. Voc. i. 20, 51.
r&aelig-acute;dere, es; m. I. a reader, one who reads :-- R&aelig-acute;dere lector, Wrt. Voc. i. 72, 6 : Ælfc. Gr. 9, 21; Som. 10, 40. Be ðære wucan r&aelig-acute;dere (rédere, 7, 23). Gebróðra gereorde ne sceal beón bútan háligre r&aelig-acute;dinge. Ne nán ne gedyrstl&aelig-acute;ce, ðæt hé f&aelig-acute;rlíce bóc gelæcce and ð&aelig-acute;r bútan foresceáwunge onginne tó r&aelig-acute;denne, ac ðære wucan r&aelig-acute;dere on ðone Sunnandæg mid bletsunge hit beginne ... Nánes mannes stefn gehýred ne sý bútan ðæs r&aelig-acute;deres ánes, R. Ben. 62, 2-15. II. a reader, scholar :-- Swá swá ða geleáfullan r&aelig-acute;deras hit gesetton, Lchdm. iii. 256, 21. III. a reader, lector, the second of the seven orders :-- Seofon hádas syndon gesette on cyrcan . . . óðer is lector .... Lector is r&aelig-acute;dere, ðe r&aelig-acute;d on Godes cyrcan, and biþ ð&aelig-acute;rtó gehádod ðæt hé bodige Godes word, L. Ælfc. C. 10-12; Th. ii. 346, 25-32. Rédere réderes forlonge foreboderes ł ceigeras fruma from wítgum ð&aelig-acute;m is gecuoedin ceig lector; lectores dudum praecones vel clamatores, initium a prophetis, quibus dicitur, Clama, Rtl. 194, 1-4. IV. a reader of riddles, a diviner (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, VI a) :-- Wiccum, fram r&aelig-acute;derum pythonibus, Hpt. Gl. 504, 67, v. bóc-r&aelig-acute;dere.
r&aelig-acute;de-sceamol, es; m. A reading-bench (?) ; a 'ready,' prepared bench, bench with furniture, a couch, cf. Icel. reiðu-stóll, and see rád :-- On r&aelig-acute;descamole in pulpito, Wrt. Voc. ii. 45, 3. R&aelig-acute;descamelas fulchra (cf. fulcra eal bedreáf, Wrt. Voc. i. 59, 33 : fulcris, thoris, lectis, Wülck. Gl. 245, 28), 36, 36.
r&aelig-acute;des-mann, es; m. I. a counsellor, adviser, councillor :-- Ealle ðæs cynges r&aelig-acute;desmen, Chart. Th. 330, 8 : Chr, 1039; Erl. 167, 19. II. a steward, manager :-- Æt Steorran ðe ðá wæs ðæs kinges r&aelig-acute;desman, Chart. Th. 339,12. [Icel. ráðs-maðr a manager, counsellor, steward.]
r&aelig-acute;desn (?), e; f. A cluster of grapes; bacido [cf. clyster bacido, botrus, Wrt. Voc. i. 33, 31] :-- Rédisn vacedo (in a list de lignis), Wrt. Voc. i. 285, 43. Rédisnae bacidones (cf. raedinne bacidones, 43, 26o : r&aelig-acute;denne, Wrt. Voc. ii. 10, 59), Txts. 44, 1.
r&aelig-acute;destre, an; f. A female reader :-- Rédestre, Ælfc. Gr. 9, 21; Som. 10, 40. R&aelig-acute;dystre, 9, 64; Som. 13, 63. R&aelig-acute;distre, Wrt. Voc. i. 72, 7.
r&aelig-acute;de-wíga. v. r&aelig-acute;de-cempa.
r&aelig-acute;d-fæst; adj. Wise, prudent :-- Se deófol gemacaþ ðæt se man þurh leáse hiwunge déþ swylce hé r&aelig-acute;dfæst sý ðe r&aelig-acute;des ne gýmeþ the devil causes the man by a false show to act as if he were wise, who cares not for wisdom, Wulfst. 53, 9. Ðæt ic on ðínum rihte r&aelig-acute;dfæst lifige, Ps. Th. 142, 11. Ðínes ríces r&aelig-acute;dfæst wulder gloriam magnificentiae regni tui, 144, 12. Him in gást becwom r&aelig-acute;dfæst sefa, Cd. Th. 257, 3; Dan. 652 : Exon. 468, 23; Hy. 5, 4. Se ðe symle byþ r&aelig-acute;dfest, Wald. 108; Vald. 2, 26 : Cd. Th. 90, 20; Gen. 1498. Áris and gereorda ðé mid
r&aelig-acute;dfæstum móde, Homl. Skt. i. 18, 185. Se r&aelig-acute;d wæs &aelig-acute;fre on his r&aelig-acute;dfæstum geþance, Ælfc. T. Grn. 2, 5. Ðæt hig mágon árísan, gif hig r&aelig-acute;dfæste beóþ, 19, 5. Rincas r&aelig-acute;dfæste, Exon. Th. 347, 15; Sch. 13. Cf. r&aelig-acute;d-leás.
r&aelig-acute;dfæstlíce. v. un-r&aelig-acute;dfæstlíce.
r&aelig-acute;dfæstness, e; f. Readiness to follow good counsel, adherence to right courses :-- Eahta sweras syndon ðe rihtlícne cynedóm up wegaþ ... r&aelig-acute;dfæstnes (persuabilitas), L. I. P. 3; Th. ii. 306, 20.
r&aelig-acute;d-findende furnishing counsel, advising :-- R&aelig-acute;dfindende consulentes, Wrt. Voc. ii. 24, 29. Cf. r&aelig-acute;d-hycgende.
r&aelig-acute;dgasram glosses hyadas, Txts. 69, 1035.
r&aelig-acute;d-geþeaht, es; n. Counsel :-- Consilium, ðæt is r&aelig-acute;dgeþeht on Englisc, Wulfst. 51, 6. Elene héht Eusebium on r&aelig-acute;dgeþeaht gefetian, Elen. Kmbl. 2101; El. 1052. Héht gefetigean tó rúne ðone ðe r&aelig-acute;dgeþeaht þurh gleáwe miht georne cúðe, 2322; El. 1162.
r&aelig-acute;d-gifa, an; m. One who gives counsel, a counsellor, councillor, adviser; mostly of the king's advisers; it also translates consul :-- R&aelig-acute;dgifa consiliator, Wrt. Voc. i. 50, 1. Stígand ðe wæs ðæs cinges r&aelig-acute;dgifa and his handprést, Chr. 1051; Th. i. 317, col. 2. R&aelig-acute;dgifan consulem, Germ. 397, 560. Ðis sindon ða ger&aelig-acute;dnessa ðe Engla r&aelig-acute;dgifan gecuran and gecw&aelig-acute;dan, L. Eth. vi. 1; Th. i. 314, 3. Ealle ðæs kyninges r&aelig-acute;dgyfan (conciliarii), Chart. Th. 326, 7. Ðone r&aelig-acute;d ðe ic mid mínum r&aelig-acute;dgyfum ger&aelig-acute;dd hæbbe, 307, 10. R&aelig-acute;dgifena juris peritorum, Hpt. Gl. 524, 69. [Cleope nu to ræde þine ræd&yogh;iuen gode, Laym. 11615. O. Sax. rád-ge&b-bar;o : O. Frs. réd jeva : O. H. Ger. rát-gebo : Icel. ráð-gjafi.] Cf. r&aelig-acute;d-bora and next word.
r&aelig-acute;d-gift glosses consulatus, senatus in the following instances :-- R&aelig-acute;dgiftes consulates, Hpt. Gl. 412, 64. R&aelig-acute;dgyft senatu, Hymn. Surt. 105, 34. R&aelig-acute;dgifte senatum, Germ. 398, 108.
r&aelig-acute;d-hycgende; part. Having wise counsel in the mind, prudent, sagacious :-- Ðú ðé ánne genim tó gesprecan symle r&aelig-acute;dhycgende, Exon. Th. 301, 28; Fä. 26.
r&aelig-acute;dic (rædic ?), es; m. A radish :-- R&aelig-acute;dic raphanum vel radix, Wrt. Voc. i. 31, 37 : vermenaca, 68, 65 : hierobotanim, ii. 43, 52. Rédic, Lchdm. ii. 276, 10. Syle ðane r&aelig-acute;dic tó þicganne . . . se r&aelig-acute;dic, 286, 10-14. Hr&aelig-acute;dic, iii. 20, 26. Genim hr&aelig-acute;dic nyðeweardne, 46, 1. [O. H. Ger. rátih, retih : M. H. Ger. retich : Ger. rettich. From Lat. radic-em.]
r&aelig-acute;ding, e; f. I. reading :-- Bisceopes dægweorc. Ðæt biþ mid rihte his gebedu &aelig-acute;rest, and ðonne his bócweorc, r&aelig-acute;ding, L. I. P. 8; Th. ii. 314, 19. Æmtigaþ eów tó r&aelig-acute;dinge vacate lectioni, hé beg&aelig-acute;þ his r&aelig-acute;dinge vacuus est lectionibus, Ælfc. Gr. 33; Som. 37, 14. Ðæs ðe ic on r&aelig-acute;dinge ne mihte fullíce ásmeágan, Wulfst. 65, 22. Beó ðú ábisgad ymbe r&aelig-acute;dinge attende lectioni, Past. 22, 1; Swt. 169,17. I a. a reading, a single act of reading :-- Ofthr&aelig-acute;dlíce r&aelig-acute;dinga háligra bóca, L. E. I. 2; Th. ii. 404, 2. Capitula r&aelig-acute;dinga, R. Ben. 43, 2. II. what is read, reading, a passage in a book, a lesson :-- Ðis Englise &aelig-acute;týwþ hwæt seó foresette r&aelig-acute;ding (passage) m&aelig-acute;nþ, Anglia viii. 298, 9. Seó r&aelig-acute;ding cwyþ ðæt ð&aelig-acute;r ys gyt on &aelig-acute;lcum tácne healftíd, 298, 31 : 300, 32 : 309, 1. Sý án r&aelig-acute;dincg ger&aelig-acute;d of ðære ealdan cýðnesse let one lesson from the Old Testament be read, R. Ben. 34, 12. Agustinus ús onwreáh ðissere r&aelig-acute;dinge (the lesson for the day) andgit, Homl. Th. ii. 384, 21. Swá swá gé gehýrdon on ðissere r&aelig-acute;dinge (the homily which precedes), Homl. Skt. i. 11, 284. Hé lufode hálige r&aelig-acute;dinge ... ealle his geféran sceolde sealmas leornian oððe sume r&aelig-acute;dinge, Swt. A. S. Rdr. 97, 62-65. Gé sculon singan sunnanúhtan &aelig-acute;fre nigon ræpsas mid nigon r&aelig-acute;dingum, L. Ælfc. P. 44; Th. ii. 384, 5. Man þreó r&aelig-acute;dinga r&aelig-acute;de, R. Ben. 33. 14. Wé willaþ on ðisre stówe ða seofon r&aelig-acute;dinga (passages) áwrítan ðe ymbe ða seofon geár synd gedihte ... Ðás r&aelig-acute;dinga syndon wíde cúðe, Anglia viii. 314, 18-22. III. rule, government (v. r&aelig-acute;dan, IV) :-- Hæfdon sume mid áþum gefæstnod ðæt hí on hire r&aelig-acute;dinge (r&aelig-acute;denne, other MSS.) beón woldon, Chr. 918; Erl. 105, 30. v. béc-, bóc-, pistol-r&aelig-acute;ding.
r&aelig-acute;ding-bóc; f. A book containing the lessons, a lectionary :-- Se mæssepreóst sceal habban ða w&aelig-acute;pna tó ðam gástlícum weorce... ðæt synd ða hálgan béc ... r&aelig-acute;dingbóc, L. Ælfc. C. 21; Th. ii. 350, 14. ii. forealdode r&aelig-acute;dingbéc swíðe wáke (cf. ii. sumerr&aelig-acute;dingbéc and i. winterr&aelig-acute;dingbóc, 16), Chart. Th. 430, 30. v. Maskell's Monumenta, vol, i. C. 3.
r&aelig-acute;ding-gewrit, r&aelig-acute;distre. v. r&aelig-acute;den-gewrit, r&aelig-acute;destre.
r&aelig-acute;d-leás; adj. I. without counsel, unwise, inconsiderate, rash, ill-advised :-- Rédeleás preceps, Ælfc. Gr. 9, 55; Som. 13, 27. Gleáw ne wæs gumríces weard, réðe and r&aelig-acute;dleás, Cd. Th. 226, 26; Dan. 177. II. without wise direction, in confusion :-- Ðá ðis (the destruction of certain ships) cúð wæs tó ðám óðrum scipon ... wæs ðá swilc hit eall r&aelig-acute;dleás w&aelig-acute;re it was as if there were no counsel anywhere, as if everything was in confusion, Chr. 1009; Erl. 142, 9. III. lacking what is advantageous or beneficial, miserable, desolate (v. r&aelig-acute;d, IV) :-- Gé Godes cræfta nán þing ne gýmaþ, ðý is folces forfaren máre ðonne scolde oððe þearf w&aelig-acute;re, and for ðam hit wearð swá r&aelig-acute;dleás ðe hit Godes beboda forgýmde the people is become so miserable, because it neglected God's commandments, Wulfst. 46, 20. Ðæt r&aelig-acute;dleáse hof (hell), Cd. Th. 3, 32; Gen. 44. [Nabbich in me wisdom ... and am redleas ... Drihten ase þu ert redlease (gen. pl.) red, red me þet am redles O. E. Homl, i. 211, 32 -213, 1. Nis nevre mon redles Ar his heorte beo witles, O. and N. 691.] [O. H. Ger. ráti-ló sabsque consilio : Ger. rat-los : Icel. ráð-lauss shiftless, confused. foolish.]
R&AElig-acute;D-LÍC - R&AElig-acute;RAN
r&aelig-acute;d-líc; adj. Advisable :-- Him ðá r&aelig-acute;dlecre geþúhte ðæt hé wið óðerne here friþ genáme ðæt hé ðone óðerne ðé iéð ofercuman mehtc proviso ad tempus consilio, unum denuntiato bello adpetit, alterum pacta pace suspendit, Ors. 3, 1; Swt. 96, 15 : 4, 13; Swt. 212, 16. Tó smeágenne wið his witan hwet heom eallum r&aelig-acute;dlícost þúhte, Chr. 1006; Erl. 141, 4. [Icel. ráð-ligr.]
r&aelig-acute;d-líce; adv. I. wisely, skilfully, cleverly :-- Hé r&aelig-acute;dlíce slóh swá hé hine (the ball) n&aelig-acute;fre feallan ne lét, Ap. Th. 13, 5. Ðæt hé meahte ðæt folc ðý wíslícor and ðý r&aelig-acute;dlícor l&aelig-acute;ran, Past. 18, 2; Swt. 131, 18. II. advisedly, deliberately, designedly, on purpose :-- R&aelig-acute;dlíce consulto, Ælfc. Gr. 38; Som. 41, 35. On ðám gemótan ðeáh r&aelig-acute;dlíce wurðan on namcúðan stówan, L. Eth. ix. 37; Th. i. 348, 17. [Icel. ráðliga cleverly.] v. án-, fæst-, un-r&aelig-acute;dlíce.
r&aelig-acute;d-mægen, es; n. Beneficial force (?), force that is productive of good or abundant good (?), cf. lof-mægen (v. r&aelig-acute;d, IV) :-- Ðá wæs wæstmum áweaht world onspreht ... r&aelig-acute;dmægne oferþeaht the world was aroused to fruitful life, and overspread by productive force, Exon. Th. 353, 10; Reim. 10.
r&aelig-acute;dness, es; f. I. readiness, promptness :-- R&aelig-acute;dnis (hrædnis?) pernicitas, Txts. 182, 75. On r&aelig-acute;dnysse in maturitate, Blickl. Gl. Ðone þóþor mid swiftre r&aelig-acute;dnesse geslegene ongeán gesænde tó ðam plegendan cynge, Ap. Th. 13, 4. R&aelig-acute;dnisse (hrædnisse ?) concursionibus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 105, 24. R&aelig-acute;dnessum, 15, 26. II. an arrangement, agreement, condition :-- Ðæt ðeós ger&aelig-acute;dnis stondon móte in écnesse, and ðis syndon ðara manna naman ðe æt ðære rédnisse w&aelig-acute;ron, Chart. Th. 168, 30. v. ge-r&aelig-acute;dness, r&aelig-acute;de.
r&aelig-acute;d-rípe (hræd- ?) ; adj. Soon ripe, premature :-- R&aelig-acute;drípe wæstm praecoquus fructus, Wrt. Voc. i. 39, 22. R&aelig-acute;drípe wínberige praecoquae, 38, 61.
r&aelig-acute;d-snotor; adj. Wise in counsel, prudent, sagacious :-- N&aelig-acute;fre ic s&aelig-acute;lidan sélran métte r&aelig-acute;dsnotteran, Andr. Kmbl. 946; An. 473. [Icel. ráð-snotr sagacious.]
r&aelig-acute;d-þeahtende; part. Consulting, deliberating :-- Ges&aelig-acute;ton sigerófe r&aelig-acute;dþeahtende ymb ða róda þreó, Elen. Kmbl. 1734; El. 869: 895; El. 449. Cf. r&aelig-acute;d-hycgende and next word.
r&aelig-acute;d-þeahtere, es; m. A counsellor, adviser :-- Ða (the senators) w&aelig-acute;ron simbel binnan Rómebyrg wuniende, tó ðon ðæt hié heora r&aelig-acute;dþeahteras w&aelig-acute;ron, Ors. 2, 4; Swt. 72, 3. Ðara twentigra monna ðe hé him tó fultume hæfde ácoren, ðæt his r&aelig-acute;dþeahteras w&aelig-acute;ron viginti viros sibi consilii causa legerat, 6, 2; Swt. 256, 3.
r&aelig-acute;d-þeahtung, e; f. Counsel :-- Hé wæs gem&aelig-acute;rsad ofer ealle óðere cyningas &aelig-acute;gðer ge mid his miclan fultume ge mid his r&aelig-acute;dþeahtunge ge mid his wígcræfte ob magnitudinem virium consiliorumque summam belli nomenque traduxit, Ors. 4. 1; Swt. 154, 27.
r&aelig-acute;d-wægn, es; m. A vehicle, chariot :-- Hé hiene hét iernan beforan his r&aelig-acute;dw&aelig-acute;ne ante vehiculum ejus, Ors. 6, 30; Swt. 280, 13. Cf. Icel. reið-skjótr, but see also hræd-wægn.
r&aelig-acute;d-wita, an; m. A counsellor, one wise in counsel :-- Ríce r&aelig-acute;dwitan, Dom. L. 18, 298.
r&aelig-acute;fan (?) ; p. te To involve, wrap :-- Hí weorþaþ ger&aelig-acute;fte (ger&aelig-acute;pte (?) cf. gereæpeð (-r&aelig-acute;ped ?) Met. 25, 48) mid ðære unrótnesse, Bt. 37, 1; Fox 186, 21. [Icel. reifa to swaddle.] v. ráfian.
ræfnan; p. de. I. to endure, suffer, undergo :-- Ræfnde perpetitur, Wrt. Voc. i. 66, 66. Ðeáh hé deáþes cwealm ræfnan sceolde, Exon. Th. 240, 24; Ph. 643. II. to do, perform, accomplish, carry out :-- Ða ðe ræfnaþ hér wordum and weorcum wuldorcyninges láre, 149, 20; Gú. 764 : 139, 17; Gú. 594. Neáh is Drihten eallum ðe his willan hér wyrceaþ georne and his hyge swylce elne ræfnaþ, Ps. Th. 144, 19. Hié ðæt ófstum miclum ræfndon, Judth. Thw. 21, 9; Jud. l1. Ræfn elne ðis, ðæt ðú n&aelig-acute;fre f&aelig-acute;cne weorð freónde ðínum, Exon. Th. 302, 3; Fä. 30. v. á-ræfnan and cf. dreógan for the same two meanings.
ræfnendlíc, ræfnian, ræfniendlíc, refsan. v. un-áræfnendlíc, á-ræfnian, on-ræfniendlíc, ræpsan.
ræfter, es; m. A rafter, beam :-- Ræfter tignum, Wrt. Voc. i. 26, 40 : 82, 14 : 290, 5. Reftras amites, Txts. 36, 11. Ræftras, Wrt. Voc. ii. 6, 58 : anses, 10, 56. Reafteres vel latta asseres, i. 58, 35. Mycelne aad on beámum and on ræftrum and on wágum and on watelum and on þacum congeriem trabium, tignorum, parietum, virgeorum & tecti fenei, Bd. 3, 16; S. 542, 22. &AElig-acute;rest man ásmeáþ ðæs húses stede, and eác man ðæt timber beheáwþ, and ða syllan man fægere gefégþ, and ða beámas gelegþ, and ða ræftras tó ðære fyrste gefæstnaþ, Anglia viii. 324, 7-9.
r&aelig-acute;ge, an; f. A roe, a wild she-goat :-- R&aelig-acute;ge caprea, Wrt. Voc. i. 78, 31 : capriole, ii. 129, 59. Hr&aelig-acute;ge damula vel caprea, i. 22, 65. Ráge, ii. 16, 80. Mýnster ðe is nemned æt Hrége heáfde (ad Caprae caput), Bd. 3, 21; S. 551, 18. Ic gefeó r&aelig-acute;gan capio capreas, Coll. Monast. Th. 21, 31. R&aelig-acute;gean (r&aelig-acute;gan, MS. B.), Lchdm. i. 166, 24. [O. H. Ger. reia caprea.] v. rá,
ræge-reósa, an; m. : -reóse (?); f. A ridge of muscles at the side of the spine running up the back :-- L&aelig-acute;cedómas wið rægereósan sáre, Lchdm. ii. 14, 26. Wið rægereósan, rúdan swá gréne, seóþ on ele and on weaxe, smire mid ðone rægereósan. Eft nim gáte h&aelig-acute;r, sméc under ða bréc wið ðás rægereósan, 146, 1-3. Be ðam nafolan and ðam rægereósan and bæcþearme, 230, 26. Biþ ðæt sár fram ðam nafolan óþ ðone milte and on ða winestran rægereósan, and gecymþ æt ðam bæcþearme, 232, 3-6. v. Lchdm. ii. Glossary.
r&aelig-acute;g-hár; adj. Grey like the goat (v. r&aelig-acute;ge) :-- Oft ðæs wág gebád r&aelig-acute;ghár and reádfáh ríce æfter óðrum oft did its wall, grey and redstained, see change of rule, Exon. Th. 476, 19; Ruin. 10.
rægiming (?) :-- A clapping of the wings (?) :-- Pullorum cocca, plausu blisse laetitiae fiðerslehte (in margin) rægiminge, Hpt. Gl. 518, 51-54.
rægu. v. ragu.
r&aelig-acute;man. v. á-r&aelig-acute;man.
r&aelig-acute;ming (?) :-- Heofenlícre r&aelig-acute;minge celibea Tempe, Wrt. Voc. ii. 130, 54.
rænc. v. renc.
r&aelig-acute;pan; p. te To bind (with a rope), make captive :-- Hí férdon &aelig-acute;ghwiðer and úre earme folc r&aelig-acute;pton (rýpton, MS. C.) and slógan (cf. r&aelig-acute;pling), Chr. 1011; Erl. 145, 6. Cyspan and mid racentan r&aelig-acute;pen, Met. 26, 78. [Icel. reipa to fasten with a rope.] v. ge-r&aelig-acute;pan.
r&aelig-acute;ping. v. next two words.
r&aelig-acute;pling, r&aelig-acute;ping, es; m. One bound, a captive, prisoner, criminal :-- Wæs ðá r&aelig-acute;pling se ðe &aelig-acute;r wæs Angelcynnes heáfod (of archbishop Ælfheah taken captive by the Danes), Chr. 1011; Erl. 145, 19. Hé (St. Paul) wæs ðyder (to Rome) r&aelig-acute;pling gel&aelig-acute;ded, Blickl. Homl. 173, 7. R&aelig-acute;plinga damnatorum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 26, 54. Se wæs gebunden mid ðám r&aelig-acute;plingum qui cum seditiosis erat vinctus, Mk. Skt. 15, 7. On cweartern ð&aelig-acute;r man ðæs cyninges r&aelig-acute;plingas heóld, Gen. 39, 20. R&aelig-acute;plingas his vinctos suos, Ps. Spl. 68, 32. R&aelig-acute;plingas unbindan, Dóm. L. 4, 48. Ic geseah r&aelig-acute;pingas in ræced fergan . . . ða w&aelig-acute;ron genamne nearwum bendum, gefeterade fæsta tógædre (two buckets of a draw-well), Exon. Th. 435, 1; Rä. 53, 1.
r&aelig-acute;pling-weard, es; m. A keeper of prisoners :-- Réplingcweardes collegiati, Wrt. Voc. i. 18, 45. R&aelig-acute;pingweardas collegiati, ii. 134, 52.
ræps, reps, es; m. A response (in the service of the church) :-- &AElig-acute;fengebed vespertinum officium, reps responsorium, r&aelig-acute;ding lectio, Wrt. Voc. i. 28, 32. Sý án r&aelig-acute;ding ger&aelig-acute;d, and án swýðe scort ræps æfterfylige, R. Ben. 34, 53. Án r&aelig-acute;ding, æfter ðam reps (ræps, MSS. O. F. : ryps, MS. T.), ymen, fers and lofsang, 36, 21. Æfter ðæm glorian ðæs feórþan repses (ræpses, MS. O.), 35, 18. Man þreó r&aelig-acute;dinga r&aelig-acute;de and þrý ræpsas. Æt ðam þriddan repse singe se sangere 'Gloria Patri,' 33, 14-16 : 35, 8-10. On ðisum dagum wé forl&aelig-acute;taþ on úrum repsum 'Gloria Patri,' Homl. Th. ii. 224, 26. Gé sculon singan sunnanúhtan &aelig-acute;fre nigon ræpsas mid nigon r&aelig-acute;dingum, L. Ælfc. P. 44; Th. ii. 384, 5.
ræpsan; p. te To seize (?), to reprove (?) :-- Raebsid uuaes, repset uaes, ræpsit wæs interceptum est (cf. á-raepsid, -repsit interceptum, 511), Txts, 68, 523. Raefsed, refset, raefsit interpellari, 70, 526. Refsede intercepit, 69, 1082. Cf. Fornoom intercepit, 71, 1083. Arásed intercéptum, 69, 1067. Árásed wæs interceptus est, Wrt. Voc. ii. 46, 31. [O. H. Ger. refsan; p. rafsta corripere, increpare, arguere, reprehendere.]
ræpsung, e; f. I. seizing (?), reproving (?) :-- Raepsung interceptio (v. preceding word, and cf. O. H. Ger. rafsunga correptio, invectio, increpatio), Txts. 69, 1068. II. an interval :-- Seó niht hæfþ seofan d&aelig-acute;las ... Óðer is uesperum, ðæt is &aelig-acute;fen, ðonne se &aelig-acute;fensteorra betwux ðære repsunge æteówaþ, Lchdm. iii. 244, 1. Vesperum ðæt ys &aelig-acute;fen oððe hrepsung, Anglia viii. 319, 28.
r&aelig-acute;ran; p. de To cause to rise, to rear, raise. I. to lift up, move from a lower to a higher position :-- Hé ús tó roderum up hl&aelig-acute;dre r&aelig-acute;rde, Exon. Th. 437, 11; Rä. 56, 6. Hí tó heofenum up hl&aelig-acute;dræ r&aelig-acute;rdon, Cd. Th. 101, 1; Gen. 1675. Hié tó gúþe gárwudu r&aelig-acute;rdon, 198, 20; Exod. 325. R&aelig-acute;re up ðín heáfod and geseoh ðis ðæt Simon déþ, Blickl. Homl. 187, 35. II. to raise (a building) :-- Ðú r&aelig-acute;rst hús domum aedifices, Deut. 28, 30. Hí wíbed setton neáh ðam ðe Abraham &aelig-acute;ror r&aelig-acute;rde, Cd. Th. 113, 7; Gen. 1883. Ðæt beácen (the tower of Babel) ðe r&aelig-acute;ran ongunnon Adames eaforan, 101, 13; Gen. 1681. Ongunnon him bytlian and heora burh r&aelig-acute;ran, 113, 1; Gen. 1880. III. to set up, establish (a law, institution, etc.) :-- God sibbe r&aelig-acute;reþ éce tó ealdre engla and monna, Exon. Th. 43, 16; Cri. 689. Hé Cristes cyricean on his ríce geornlíce timbrede and r&aelig-acute;rde ecclesiam Christi in regno suo multum diligenter aedificare ac dilatare curavit, Bd. 3, 3; S. 525, 37. Man unriht r&aelig-acute;rde and unlaga manege, Wulfst. 156, 13. Ðonne r&aelig-acute;re man cyninges munde, ðæt is ðæt hý ealle ðam sémende syllan ðæt cyninges mund stande, L. E. G. 13; Th. i. 174, 20. Se ðe unlage r&aelig-acute;re oððe undóm gedéme, L. C. S. 15; Th. i. 384, 9. Ys his handgeweorc ryhte dómas ða hé r&aelig-acute;ran wyle opera manuum ejus judicium, Ps. Th. 110, 5. IV. to raise, offer (a prayer) :-- Hyra þeódnes dóm ðæt hié to ðam beácne (the golden image) gebedu r&aelig-acute;rde, Cd. Th. 227, 24; Dan. 191. V. to raise, begin, give rise to, excite (ill feeling) :-- R&aelig-acute;rde exagitabat, Wrt. Voc. ii. 30, 22. Oft hí þræce r&aelig-acute;rdon ... feóndscype r&aelig-acute;rdon oft were their violence and enmity roused, Exon. Th. 243, 18-22; Jul. 12-14. Háteþ þræce r&aelig-acute;ran ... ðæt hí úsic binden and in bælwylme swingen, 262, 16; Jul. 333. F&aelig-acute;hþe r&aelig-acute;ran, 113, 14; Gú. 157. Ne cúðon firena fremman ... elles ne ongunnon r&aelig-acute;ran on roderum nymþe riht and sóð, Cd. Th. 2, 18; Gen. 21. Geflitu r&aelig-acute;ran, Elen. Kmbl. 884; El. 443. Sæce r&aelig-acute;ran, 1879; El. 941. VI. to rouse, excite :-- Saga hwá mec r&aelig-acute;re ðonne ic restan ne mót, oððe hwá mec stæððe ðonne ic stille beom, Exon. Th. 387, 2; Rä. 4, 73. VII. to raise, elevate, exalt, promote :-- Gif ðú sóðne God lufast and his lof r&aelig-acute;rest, 245, 22; Jul. 48 : 103, 17; Cri. 1681 : 111, 23; Gú. 131. Se &aelig-acute;rest æðelinga éðelþrym rýmde and r&aelig-acute;rde, Cd. Th. 98, 24; Gen. 1635. Uton beón á úrum hláforde holde, and &aelig-acute;fre eallum mihtum his wurðscipe r&aelig-acute;ran, L. C. E. 20; Th. i. 372, 9 : Wulfst. 119, 14. Hú neáh ðære tíde w&aelig-acute;re ðætte ða bróðru árísan sceolden and Godes lof r&aelig-acute;ran and heora úhtsang singan quam prope esset hora qua fratres ad dicendas Domino laudes nocturnal excitari deberent, Bd. 4. 24; S. 599, 4. [Goth. raisjan : Icel. reisa.] v. á-r&aelig-acute;ran.
R&AElig-acute;REND - RAM-GEALLA
r&aelig-acute;rend, r&aelig-acute;rness. v. á-r&aelig-acute;rend, -r&aelig-acute;rness.
r&aelig-acute;s, es; m. I. a race, swift or violent running, rush :-- Wæs se þridda hlýp, rodorcyninges r&aelig-acute;s ðá hé on róde ástág, Exon. Th. 45, 30; Cri. 727. Micle r&aelig-acute;se (magno impetu) worn tódrifen wæs on s&aelig-acute;, Mk. Skt. Rush. 5, 13. Mycelum r&aelig-acute;se, Lk. Skt. 8, 33. Ðæt hors sum slóg on ðam wege mid swíðran r&aelig-acute;se (valentiore impetu) oferhleóp, Bd. 5, 6; S. 619, 17. Ongeán ðam r&aelig-acute;se ðæs forþgotenan streámes contra impetum fluvii decurrentis, 5, 10; S. 625, 7. Hé hét hwílon ða hundas ætstandan ðe urnon on ðam r&aelig-acute;se deórum getenge he sometimes ordered the dogs to stop that were running at full speed close upon the game, Homl. Th. ii. 514, 25. II. an onset, attack :-- Beadumægnes r&aelig-acute;s, Cd. Th. 198, 28; Exod. 329. Hit ofslóh mínra þegna xxvi. áne r&aelig-acute;se (in one onslaught), Nar. 15, 25. Ðá wearð líg tólýsed, leád wíde sprong, hæleþ wurdon acle for ðý r&aelig-acute;se, Exon. Th. 277, 27; Jul. 587. Hé gúðe r&aelig-acute;s mid his freádryhtne fremman sceolde, Beo. Th. 5246; B. 2626. Gúðe r&aelig-acute;sum, 4702; B. 2356. [Laym. ræs, res, reas an attack, onslaught : Allit. Pms, to run in on a res to rush in : Icel. rás; f. a race, running.] v. beadu-, deáþ-, feónd-, gár-, gúþ-, hand-, heaðo-, hilde-, m&aelig-acute;g-, mægen-, on-, scyte-, sweord-, syn-, wæl-r&aelig-acute;s.
r&aelig-acute;s (?), -we; f. Counsel, deliberation :-- Ðonne merestreámas meotudes r&aelig-acute;swum (or from r&aelig-acute;swa ?) onwealcaþ, Exon. Th. 193, 24; Az. 126. And see r&aelig-acute;s-bora, r&aelig-acute;swian.
r&aelig-acute;san; p. de To rush, move violently or impetuously; inruere :-- R&aelig-acute;sde inruit, Wrt. Voc. ii. 111, 56. I. of actual movement :-- Seó h&aelig-acute;tu r&aelig-acute;sde on ða ðe ðæt fýr &aelig-acute;lde, Bd. 3, 16; S. 543, 9. Hé, getogene ðý w&aelig-acute;pne, r&aelig-acute;sde on ðone cyning, 2, 9; S. 511, 22. Hé út r&aelig-acute;sde on ðone æþeling, Chr. 755; Erl. 48, 34. Se stranga wind ð&aelig-acute;r on r&aelig-acute;sde, Shrn. 81, 32. Hit on ús and on úre wícstówe r&aelig-acute;sde, Nar. 15, 20 : Beo. Th. 5373; B. 2690. Hiá r&aelig-acute;sdon (inruerent) on hine, Mk. Skt. Lind. Rush. 3, 10. Hundas r&aelig-acute;sdon on ðone apostol, Blickl. Homl. 181, 21. Hié r&aelig-acute;sdon on gífrum grápum, Andr. Kmbl. 2670; An. 1336. W&aelig-acute;ron hý reówe tó r&aelig-acute;sanne gífrum grápum, Exon. Th. 126, 27; Gú. 377. R&aelig-acute;sed eode impetu abiit, Mt. Kmbl. Rush. 8, 32. II. of violent action, to proceed against with violence, to assault, attack :-- Se hláford ne scrífþ freónde ne feónde, ac hé réðigmód r&aelig-acute;st on gehwilcne wédehunde gelícost (cf. se ne murnþ náuþer ne friénd ne fiénd ðe má ðe wédende hund, Bt. 37. 1; Fox 186, 7-8), Met. 25, 17. Hine (deáþ) r&aelig-acute;scþ on gífrum grápum, Exon. Th. 161, 34; Gú. 968. Hú longe on r&aelig-acute;saþ (inruitis) gé on men, Ps. Surt. 61, 4. On r&aelig-acute;sdun (inruerunt) in mé stronge, 58, 4. Ðæs burhgeréfan sunu wolde r&aelig-acute;san on hí on ðæm scandhúse and hí bysmrian, Shrn. 56, l1. III. of precipitate action, to rush (into anything) :-- Oft mon biþ suíðe rempende, and r&aelig-acute;sð suíðe dollíce on &aelig-acute;lc weorc and hrædlíce, Past. 20; Swt. 149, 12. Geþence se láriów ðæt hé unwærlíce forþ ne r&aelig-acute;se on ða spr&aelig-acute;ce, 15; Swt. 95, 9. v. be-, ge-, in-, þurh-r&aelig-acute;san; f&aelig-acute;r-r&aelig-acute;sende.
r&aelig-acute;s-bora, an; m. A counsellor, one who takes thought for the public good, a leader, chief :-- R&aelig-acute;sbora (Abraham), Cd. Th. 108, 24; Gen. 1811. Andreas þanc gesægde rícum r&aelig-acute;sboran (the Deity who in disguise had guided Andrew's ship), Andr. Kmbl. 769; An. 385. Réðe r&aelig-acute;sboran (the chiefs of the Mermedonians), 277; An. 139. R&aelig-acute;fborena [r&aelig-acute;s- (?), r&aelig-acute;d- (?)] jurisperitorum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 87, 38. v. r&aelig-acute;s, and cf. r&aelig-acute;d-bora.
ræsc. v. líg-ræsc.
ræscan; p. te To move quickly (cf. rash), to quiver (of light), to glitter :-- Fér ræscendum leóhte ignis vibrante lumine, Hymn. Sort. 94, 1. v. ræsc, ræscettan.
ræscettan; p. te To crackle, make a crackling noise as fire does, to sparkle :-- Fýren líg braslaþ, ræsct and éfesteþ, Dóm. L. l0, 152. Ðæt réðe flód ræscet fýre, 12, 165. Ræscetteþ crepitat, Wrt. Voc. ii. 94, 66. Ræscetteþ, cyrmþ, scylþ crepitat, i. resonat, 136, 73. Ræscettan crepitarent, ræscettende crepitantes, 18, 9-10. Ræscetende crepitantes, 78, 10. [O. H. Ger. raskezzan scintillare, singultare.] v. preceding word.
ræscet[t]ung,e; f. Sparkling, gleaming, coruscation :-- Hræscetunga coruscationes, Hpt. Gl. 509, 31. v. líg-ræscetung and preceding word.
r&aelig-acute;sele, an; f. A conjecture, solution of a riddle :-- Gif ðú m&aelig-acute;ge réselan gesecgan, Saga hwæt hió hátte, Exon. Th. 421, 34; Rä. 40, 28. v. r&aelig-acute;swan, and cf. r&aelig-acute;dels, III.
ræsn, es; n. A plank, a ceiling :-- Ræsn asser, Ælfc. Gr. 9, 18; Som. 9, 59. Ræfter tignus, beám trabs, wáh paries, ræsn laquear, Wrt. Voc. i. 290, 5-8 : ii. 52, 4. [Goth. razn a house : Icel. rann.]
ræst, ræstan. v. rest, restan.
r&aelig-acute;swa, an; m. (a word used only in poetry). I. a counsellor :-- Cwæð ðá se ðe wæs cyninges r&aelig-acute;swa (cf. 'the king spake unto his counsellors ... They answered and said unto the king,' Dan. 3, 14), wís and wordgleáw, Cd. Th. 242, 11; Dan. 417. II. one who takes thought (for the public good), (a) a prince, king :-- Se r&aelig-acute;swa (Nebuchadnezzar), 256, 14; Dan. 640. Werodes r&aelig-acute;swa, Babilone weard, 246, 31; Dan. 487. Folca r&aelig-acute;swa, Caldea cyning, 257. 34; Dan. 667. Ealwealdan Gode, þeóda r&aelig-acute;swan, Andr. Kmbl. 3243; An. 1624, Folccyningas, leóde r&aelig-acute;swan, Cd. Th. 125, 6; Gen. 2075. (b) a leading man, chief person, leader :-- Ðá wearð forht manig folces r&aelig-acute;swa many a chief man among the Mermedonians, Andr. Kmbl. 2174; An. 1088. Gesetton Sennar leóda r&aelig-acute;swan leófum mannum heora, 99, 34; Gen. 1656 : 100, 25; Gen. 1669. Folces r&aelig-acute;swan (the chief men with Holofernes), Judth. Thw. 21, l0; Jud. 12. Leóda r&aelig-acute;swan (the chief men of Bethulia), 24, 8; Jud. 178. Hæleþa r&aelig-acute;swan, dugoþ dómgeorne (the high priest and his fellows), Andr. Kmbl. 1384; An. 692. Módgleáwe men, middangeardes r&aelig-acute;swan, Salm. Kmbl. 362; Sal. 180. R&aelig-acute;swan herges, the leaders of the host, Cd. Th. 192, 20; Exod. 234. Hé beforan fremede folces r&aelig-acute;swum (the chief men among the Jews), Andr. Kmbl. 1238; An. 619. [Icel. ræsir chief, captain, king.] v. ge-, here-r&aelig-acute;swa, r&aelig-acute;s-bora, and next word.
r&aelig-acute;swan, r&aelig-acute;swian, r&aelig-acute;sian, résian; p. ede, ode To think, suppose, suspect, consider, conjecture :-- Tó ð&aelig-acute;m sóðum ges&aelig-acute;lþum ðe ðín mód oft ymbe r&aelig-acute;sweþ ad veram felicitatem, quam tuus somniat animus, Bt. 22, 2; Fox 78, 7. Résiaþ comminiscimus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 18, 7. Résiat, 77, 24. Hié eallneg r&aelig-acute;swaþ and ondr&aelig-acute;daþ ðæt hí mon t&aelig-acute;lan wille they are always suspecting and dreading that people want to blame them, Past. 35, 2; Swt. 239, 6. Ðú r&aelig-acute;swedest (existimasti) swíðe unryhte ðæt ic w&aelig-acute;re ðín gelíca, Ps. Th. 49, 22. Hé résade (suspicabatur) ðæt hé hæfde ðæs Cáseres &aelig-acute;rendo sum tó Breotone cyningum ... Ðá hé ongeat ðæt hit swá ne wæs swá hé résade, Bd. 4, 1; S. 564, 48-,565. 3. R&aelig-acute;swodan, sp&aelig-acute;can, w&aelig-acute;ron gemunende comminiscuntur, Wrt. Voc. ii. 24, 1. Ne réccaþ hwæt him mon ymbe r&aelig-acute;swe mala de se opinari permittunt, Past. 59, 1; Swt. 447, 28. Ðá ongan hé mid gleáwe móde þencan and r&aelig-acute;sian (résian, MS. C.) coepit sagaci animo conjicere, Bd. 3, 10; S. 534, 21 note. Résigan opinare, Wrt. Voc. ii. 115. 55. R&aelig-acute;swian conici, conari, 131, 79. Résenðe ic eom suspicatus sum, Ps. Surt. 118, 39. v. next word.
r&aelig-acute;swung, résung, e; f. Supposition, conjecture :-- R&aelig-acute;swung vel r&aelig-acute;dels conjectura, i. opinatio, estimatio, interpretatio, Wrt. Voc. ii. 133. 53. Résung conjectura, 104, 35. Résong, 77, 72. Résunge ratiunculus, 119, 14.
ræt a rat :-- Ræt raturus (in a list of animals), Wrt. Voc. i. 22, 48. [O. Du. ratta : O. H. Ger. rato; m. ratta; f. : Icel. rotta; f.]
r&aelig-acute;w, ráw, e; f. A row, line :-- Ðonon on ða r&aelig-acute;we (hedge-row); of ðære reáwe on Temese, Cod. Dip. Kmbl. v. 275, 20. Sele ðonne drincan sume on (on sume, MS.) ráwe nigon dagon nine days in succession, Lchdm. ii. 238, 10. Cf. He sende hem so muche honger and luþer geres a-rewe, R. Glouc. 252, 2. Is seid of euerich on a-rewe, A. R. 90, 10. For þre ni&yogh;tes a-rowe he sei&yogh; þat same si&yogh;t, Chron. Vilod. 68 (in Stratmann). The word also occurs in hæsel-, hege-, hlinc-, stán-, wiðig-r&aelig-acute;w, Cod. Dip. Kmbl. iii. xxxv. Cf. also ger&aelig-acute;wud féða acies, Wrt. Voc. i. 18, 26. Standaþ on geréwe, Cod. Dip. Kmbl. iii. 424, 8. Hí on ger&aelig-acute;we s&aelig-acute;ton, Homl. Skt. i. 23, 779.
rafan. v. be-rafan.
ráfian to involve, wrap up (?) cf. Icel. reifa to swaddle; or to unloose, disclose, cf. Icel. reifa to rip up, disclose. v. á-ráfian, r&aelig-acute;fan.
ráge. v. r&aelig-acute;ge.
raggig; adj. Shaggy, bristly, ragged as applied to the rough coat of a horse :-- Raggie setosa, Hpt. Gl. 524, 16. [Icel. rögg shagginess; a tuft (cf. rug-headed kernes in Macbeth); raggaðr tufted : Swed. Dan. dial. ragg rough hair : Swed. dial. raggig shaggy : Dan. dial. raggad shaggy.]
ragu, e; f. Lichen :-- Ragu mosilicum, Wrt. Voc. i. 67, 63 : mosiclum, 287, 33 : ii. 114, 18 : mossiclum, 55, 74 : mosicum, 114, 26. Rægu sedulium, 120, 46. Hæseles ragu the lichen of hazel, Lchdm. ii. 96, 2. Cristes-m&aelig-acute;l-ragu lichen off a crucifix, 346, 23. Ragu and meós (rubigo) fornymþ ealle eówre landes wæstmas, Deut. 28, 42. v. berc-, sláhþorn-ragu.
ragu-finc, es; m. The name of some bird :-- Ragofinc scutatis, scutatus, Wrt. Voc. i. 62, 44 : 281, 15 : barrulus, ii. 10, 79. Reagufinc bariulus, 101, 62.
ráha. v. rá and next word.
ráh-deór, es; n. A roe-buck :-- Ráhdeór capreus, Wrt. Voc. i. 22, 66 : capreolus, 78, 30. Ráhdeóres mearh, Lchdm. iii. 2, 25.
ram. v. ramm.
ram-gealla, an; m. Ram-gall (a plant name); menyanthes trifoliata :-- Ramgeallan ðone fágan, Lchdm. ii. 124, 13. Hramgeallo, 140, 13.
RAM-HUND - RÁRIAN
ram-hund (?) :-- De canibus quos ramhundt vocant, L. C. F. 32; Th. 1. 430, 7.
ramm, es (a wk. gen. pl. occurs); m. I. a ram :-- Ramm aries, Wrt. Voc. i. 23, 52. Ram, 78, 46. Rom berbex, ii. 12, 71 : 126, 3. Rommes blód, Cd. Th. 177, 20; Gen. 2932, Geoffra mé &aelig-acute;nne þríwintre ramm, Gen. 15, 9 : 22, 13. Beorgas w&aelig-acute;ron blíðe swá rammas, Ps. Th. 113, 6. Bringaþ him eówra ramma bearn, 28, 1 : Ps. Spl. 65, 14. Twentig rammena arietes viginti, Gen. 32, 14. Rammum gelíce, Ps. Th. 113, 4. II. an instrument for pounding or battering :-- Aries biþ ram betwux sceápum and ram tó wealgeweorce, Ælfc. Gr. 5; Som. 4, 15. Ram tó wurce aries, Wrt. Voc. i. 34, 57. Ram aries, andweorc tó wealle cimentum, wealwyrhta cimentarius, 85, 26-28. Þerscaþ ðone weall mid rammum, Past. 21; Swt. 161, 6. 'Gáþ tó mid rammum'. . . Hé bierþ rammas ymbútan ðæt mód his hiéremonna, ðonne hé him gecýð mid hú scearplícum costungum wé sint &aelig-acute;ghwonon útan behrincgde, and se weall úres mægenes þurhþyrelað mid ðan scearpan ramman (ð&aelig-acute;m scearpan rammum, Cott. MSS.) ðara costunga, Swt. 163, 10-18. [O. H. Ger. ramm aries, vervex.]
rán, es; n. Unlawful seizure of property, robbing :-- Rán quod dicunt apertam rapinam, L. W. iii. 12; Th. i. 493, 6. [Icel. rán.]
rán rained. v. rínan.
ranc; adj. I. Proud, haughty, arrogant, insolent; the word remains with a somewhat different meaning in rank, used of coarse but fertile growth :-- Gif &aelig-acute;nig man hæbbe módigne sunu and rancne (protervum) ðe nelle híran his fæder and his méder, Deut. 21, 18. Ne beón gé tó rance ne tó gylpgeorne, Wulfst. 40, 19 : 81, 15. Some munecas synd tó wlance and ealles tó rance, L. I. P. 14; Th. ii. 322, 12. Hí taliaþ ðé wyrsan for heánan gebyrdan ða ðe heora yldran on worolde ne wurdan welige ne wlance ne on l&aelig-acute;nan líffæce rance ne ríce they account the worse for humble birth, those whose forefathers were not of great wealth or of high estate in the world, nor in this poor life-space proud or rich, L. Eth. vii. 21; Th. i. 334, 4. [Forr þatt te&yogh;&yogh; shollden Crist forseon þurrh þe&yogh;&yogh;re modignesse, þatt follc, þatt haffde beon til þa heh follc and rannc on eorþe, Orm. 9622. So were theih daungerouse for wlaunke; And siththen bicom ful reulich, that thanne weren so ranke, Pol. Songs 341, 390.] II. applied to dress, showy (cf. brave in Shakspere) :-- Witaþ ðæt ne mót mid rihte nán preóst beón ne on his girlum tó ranc ne mid golde oferglæncged, L. Ælfc. P. 49; Th. i. 386, 10. Ne gé ne sceolon beón rance mid hringgum geglengede, L. Ælfc. C. 35; Th. ii. 358. 5. v. ofer-ranc. III. bold, valiant (Icel. rakkr courageous, bold) :-- Ð&aelig-acute;r mihton geseón Winceastre leódan rancne here and unearhne a host bold and fearless, Chr. 1006; Erl. 140, 26.
ranclíce; adv. I. showily (v. ranc, II) :-- Ne eówer reáf ne beó tó ranclíce gemacod, L. Ælfc. C. 35; Th. ii. 358, 6. II. boldly (v. ranc, III) :-- Ymbe ða feówer tíman wé wyllaþ cýðan iungum preóstum má þinga ðæt hig mágon ðé ranclícor ðás þing heora clericum geswutelian, Anglia viii. 312, 18. [Icel. rakk-liga boldly, valiantly.]
ranc-str&aelig-acute;t, e; f. A road in which bravery is displayed (?) :-- God ðé w&aelig-acute;pnum l&aelig-acute;t rancstr&aelig-acute;te forþ rúme wyrcan God let thee with weapons work an ample road where thy bravery was shewn (of Abraham's rescuing Lot), Cd. Th. 127, 17; Gen. 2112. v. ranc.
rand, es; m. I. a brink, edge, margin, shore :-- Árás ðá bí ronde róf oretta (cf. gesæt ðá on næsse níðheard cyning, Beo. Th. 4825 : hl&aelig-acute;w holmwylme neáh, 4814), Ben. Th. 5069; B. 2538. Of ðam fúlan bróce wið westan randes æsc to the west of the ash tree on the bank (?), Cod. Dip. B. ii. 259, 8. [Cf. later English rand border, strip, slice :-- Rawe&yogh; and rande&yogh;, Allit. Pms, 4, 105. Randes of bakun, Piers P. Crede 763. Rand a narrow stripe, Jameson. Rand the edge of the upper leather, a seam of a shoe, Bailey. Icel. rönd a stripe : Ger. rand border, edge, margin.] II. the word however is used generally of a shield, denoting the whole or part of it. (1) Denoting a part, the boss of a round shield, cf. rand-beáh and O. H. Ger. rant umbo. The word seems to have a different meaning in Icelandic : 'á fornum skjöldum var títt at skrifa rönd þá er baugr var kallaðr, ok er viðd þann baug skildir kenndir.' v. Cl. and Vig. s.v. baugr. Grein gives margo clypei as the meaning in the following passages, but umbo suits the sense : see too Worsaaé s Primeval Antiquities of Denmark, pp. 31-2 : 51-3, where instances of early shields are given :-- Rand sceal on scylde fæst fingra gebeorh a boss must be on a shield, a sure protection for fingers (which grasped the shield just behind the boss), Menol. Fox 534; Gn. C. 37. Lígýðum forborn bord wið rond the buckler against the boss burned with the flames, Beo. Th. 5339; B. 2673. (2) Denoting the whole, a shield, buckler [Icel. rönd a shield] :-- Rand dynede, campwudu clynede, Elen. Kmbl. l00; El. 50. Ðonne rond and hand on herefelda helm ealgodon, Andr. Kmbl. 18; An. 9 : 824; An. 412. Hé under rande gecranc slain he sank under his shield, Beo. Th. 2423; B. 1209. Ðæt hé mé ongeán sleá, rand geheáwe, 1368; B. 682. Siððan ic hond and rond hebban mihte since I could bear arms, 1316; B. 656. Hond rond geféng geolwe linde, 5212; B. 2609. Scyldes rond fæste gefégan wið flyge gáres to join together firmly the shield's disk against the flight of javelin, Exon, Th. 297, 11; Crä. 65. Beorhte randas, Beo. Th. 468; B. 231. Rondas regnhearde, 657; B. 326. Ðá hí on ðone Reádan S&aelig-acute; randas b&aelig-acute;ron, Ps. Th. 105, 8; Cd. Th. 199, 2; Exod. 332. Rincas randas w&aelig-acute;gon, 123, 22; Gen. 2049. Bæd ðæt hyra randan (randas ?) rihte heóldon, Byrht. Th. 132, 22; By. 20. v. bord-, calc-, gafol-, geolo-, hilde-, síd-rand.
rand-beáh, -beág, es; m. The boss of a shield or the shield itself; buculus, bucula (cf. bucula the boss of a shield, Isidore), bucularis, umbo, testudo (cf. scyld testudo, clipeus, Wrt. Voc. i. 35, 57) :-- Randbeáh umb[r]o, Wrt. Voc. i. 84, 33 : Ælfc. Gr. 9, 3; Som. 8, 34. Ísen rand-beág ferreus umbo, ii. 147, 79. Umbo randbéh vel bucula, i. 35. 29. Randbeáh buculus, 288, 13. Rondbeág, ii. 11, 37. Rondbaeg, 102, 29. Randbeág buculus vel bucularis, 126, 65. Randbeáh testudo, Ælfc. Gr. 9, 3; Som. 8, 60. Swilce lytel pricu on brádan brede oððe rondbeáh on scilde, Bt. 18, 1; Fox 62, 5. Randbeáges umbonis, Wrt. Voc. ii. 86, 83 : Hpt. Gl. 521, 8. Hrandbeága testudine, 495, 47. Under þiccum randbeáge subter densa testudine, Ælfc. Gr. 47; Som. 48, 29. Randbeág testudinem, Hpt. Gl. 423, 58. Randbeágum umbonibus, 424, 6 : Wrt. Voc. ii. 76, 45. [O. H. Ger. rant-pouc.] v. rand.
rand-burh a town that acts as a shield (?), a fortified town, a frontier town (?) :-- Ríce geréfa rondburgum weóld, eard weardade, Exon. Th. 243, 32; Jul. 19. Randbyrig (the walls formed by the waters of the Red Sea when the Israelites passed through it) w&aelig-acute;ron rofene were riven (when the Egyptians attempted to cross), Cd. Th. 207, 7; Exod. 463. Or are the walls formed by the water compared to the arrangement of the line of battle when the shields overlapped, called scild-burh q. v. ? v. next word.
rand-gebeorh a protection such as that afforded by a shield :-- Se ágend up ár&aelig-acute;rde reáde streámas in randgebeorh the Lord hath raised the Red Sea's waters as a protecting shield (cf. the waters were a wall unto them, Ex. 14, 29), Cd. Th. 196, 24; Exod. 296.
rand-hæbbend, es; m. One who has a shield, a warrior :-- Óðer n&aelig-acute;nig sélra n&aelig-acute;re rondhæbbendra, Beo. Th. 1726; B. 861.
rand-wíga, an; m. A warrior with a shield, a warrior :-- Ríce rand-wíga (Æschere), Beo. Th. 2600; B. 1298. Rófne randwígan, 3590; B.1793. Randwígena ræst (the camping of the Israelites on their march), Cd. Th. 186, 5; Exod. 134. Randwígum frætwa d&aelig-acute;lan, 171, 14; Gen. 2828.
rand-wígend, -wíggend (-wiggend ?), es; m. A warrior with a shield, a warrior :-- Rondwíggende (the men of Holofernes), Judth. Thw. 21, 9; Jud. 11 : 21, 15; Jud. 20. Nú ic gumena gehwæne ðyssa burhleóda biddan wylle randwíggendra (the people of Bethulia), 24, 14; Jud. 188 : (the descendants of Abraham), Cd. Th. 205, 13; Exod. 435.
ráp, es; m. A rope, cord, cable :-- Ráp funiculus vel funis, Wrt. Voc. i. 15, 19 : 75, 4. Ráp vel strenc funiculus, modicus funis, ii. 151, 66. Ráp rudens, i. 285, 18. Heó lét hig út mid ánum langum rápe (per funem), Jos. 2, 15. Rápas funes vel restes, Wrt. Voc. i. 56, 58 : lora, ii. 51, 40 : restes, 93, 4 : funes, Ps. Th. 118, 61. Hig hine gebundon mid twám bæstenum rápum (novis funibus) . . . Ða rápas tóburston, Jud. 15, 13-14 : 16, 9. Hwæt beóþ ða feówere f&aelig-acute;ges rápas? Gewurdene wyrda, ða beóþ ða feówere f&aelig-acute;ges rápas, Salm. Kmbl. 661-668; Sal. 331-333. Rápa nodorum, Wrt. Voc. ii. 61, 68. Rápum rudentibus, funibus, Hpt. Gl. 529, 27. Ðú gedydest ðæt wé m&aelig-acute;tan úre land mid rápum, Ps. Th. 15, 6. Swá swá hé mid gildenum rápum áhafen w&aelig-acute;re, Bd. 4, 9; S. 576, 36. Ánra gehwilc manna is gewriðen mid rápum his synna, Homl. Th. i. 208, 4. Hé worhte áne swipe of rápum (of strengum of small cords, Jn. Skt. 2, 15), 406, 7. [Goth. raip; n. : Icel. reip; n. : O. H. Ger. reif; m.] v. ancor-, bealu-, helpend-, m&aelig-acute;rels-, mæst-, met-, net-, scip-, stig-, sund-, wæl-ráp.
ráp-gang (?), es; m. Rope-dancing :-- Rápgong (MS. -gon. Cf. 1. 33, where gegon is written for gegong [v. p. 33, 65]) funambulus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 38, 36. The meaning seems to require rap-gonga (-genga ?).
ráp-gewealc (?), es; n. A coil of rope (?), a cord :-- R&aelig-acute;pe gewælc funiculum, Ps. Spl. T. 104, 10.
rápincel, es; n. A cord, string, rope :-- Rápincel funiculus, Cant. M. ad fil. 9. On rápincle tódáles in funiculo distributionis, Blickl. Gl. : Ps. Spl. 77, 60. Rápincel funiculum, 104, 10. Mín rápincel ðú ásmeádest funiculum meum investigastis, Ps. Lamb. 138, 2.
ráp-líc; adj. Of rope :-- Ráplíc funale, Germ. 399, 469.
ráre-dumla, -dumle, an; m. f. A bittern :-- Ráredumlæ onocrotalum, avis quae sonitum facit in aqua, Shrn. 29, 6. Ráradumbla onocrotalus, Wrt. Voc. i. 62, 21. Ráredumle, 280, 26 : 63, 70 : buban, 126, 61. [M. H. Ger. rór-tumel a bittern : Ger. rohr-dommel : M. Du. roes-domel. O. H. Ger. has horo-túbil, -tumil.] [Cf. for the second part of the word, dumble-dore, the name given in some places to the bee.]
rárian; p. ode. I. of human beings, to wail, lament loudly :-- Seó dreórige módor samod mid ðám lícmannum rárigende hí ástrehte æt ðæs apostoles fótum, Homl. Th. i. 66, 18. II. of other than human beings, to roar, bellow :-- Hwílum dióflu him ráredon on swá hrýðro, Shrn. 141, 10. Rárende ł bellende rugiens, Mt. Kmbl. p. 9, 14. Ðære rárigendan bombosa, Wrt. Voc. ii. 89, 8.
RÁRUNG - REÁF-LÁC
rárung, e; f. Roaring, loud cry; barritus, Wrt. Voc. ii. 10, 68 : 79, 29 : 125, 18.
rásettan; p. te To move impetuously, to rage (of fire) :-- Hé (Nero) wolde fandian, gif ðæt fýr (at the burning of Rome) meahte swá longe reád rásettan, swá hé secgan gehérde, ðæt Troia burg ofertogen hæfde léga leóhtost, Met. 9, 14. Blác rásetteþ reáda líg, reðe scríþeþ, Exon. Th. 51, 1; Cri. 809. Cf. r&aelig-acute;s.
rásian; p. ode To explore :-- Ðá w&aelig-acute;s hord rásod, onboren beága hord, Beo. Th. 4556; B. 2283. v. á-rásian.
raðe (aspirated and unaspirated forms occur, and each can alliterate; the two forms are given separately. v. hraðe); adv. Quickly, soon, at once, directly, without hesitation :-- Raðe ilico, Wrt. Voc. ii. 44, 68 :
ocius, 64, 47. Ræðe ultro, 90, 8. Heó nam raðe (cito) hyre w&aelig-acute;fels, Gen. 24, 65. Cwelle hig man raðe (statim), L. Ecg. C. 39; Th. ii. 164, 1. Ðæt hine mon slóge swá raðe swá mon hiora fiénd wolde that they should kill him as soon (with as little compunction) as they would their enemies, Ors. 1, 12; Swt. 52, 35. Ða men w&aelig-acute;ron swá raðe deáde swá ðæt yfel him an becom, 4, 5; Swt. 166, 7. Raðe ðæs directly afterwards, 3, 10; Swt. 138, 33. Héht lífes brytta leóht forþcuman ofer rúmne grund; raðe wæs gefylled heáhcininges h&aelig-acute;s, Cd. Th. 8, 13; Gen. 123 : 95, 26; Gen. 1584 : Exon. Th. 93, 15; Cri. 1526 : Beo. Th. 1453; B. 724. Ðæs cymþ raðor iste egredietur prius, Gen. 38, 28. Ne þincþ eów nó ðý raðor (none the sooner) heora genóh, Bt. 13; Fox 38, 31 : 30, 1; Fox 108, 9. Nán man hit náh tó geáhnianne raðost þinga (at the earliest), &aelig-acute;r syx mónþum æfter ðam ðe hit forstolen wæs, L. C. S. 24; Th. i. 390, 13. Swá ðæt cild raðost &aelig-acute;nig þing specan m&aelig-acute;ge as soon as ever the child can speak, Wulfst. 39, 8. Ðonne mágon wé hí swá raðosð (in the quickest manner possible) tó ryhte gecierran, Past. 32; Swt. 209, 21.
ráw. v. r&aelig-acute;w.
ráwan (?) to cut in strips (?) (v. r&aelig-acute;w.) Cf. Geráwende infindens, Wrt. Voc. ii. 91, 24. Geráwende slítende and ceorfende infindens, 47, 22. Ger&aelig-acute;wen hrægel segmentata vestis, i. 40, 10.
rawe, Wrt. Voc. ii. 128, 39. v. rupe.
reád; adj. Red :-- Reád deáh coccus, Wrt. Voc. i. 40, 40. Reád teafor minium, 46, 74. Se reáda telg, Exon. Th. 408, 21; Rä. 27, 15. Reád ruber, Wrt. Voc. ii. 119, 35 : flavum, fulvum, 108, 70 : roseus, vel rubeus, vel pheniceus, i. 46, 50 : croceus, Hpt. Gl. 524, 37. Reádde l&aelig-acute;mene fatu alsierina, Wrt. Voc. i. 41, 47. (a) Of plants or fruit :-- Reáde, wínberige ceraunis, 38, 62. Reáde clefre calta, 67, 72. R&aelig-acute;de clæfer, 288, 49. Reád clæfre, Lchdm. ii. 312, 19. Rósena reáde heápas, Dóm. L. 18, 286. Mid reádum rósum cum purpureis rosis, Hpt. Gl. 511, 4. (b) of gold :-- Reád gold aurum obrizum, Wrt. Voc. i. 38, 33 : Met. 19, 6 : Cd. Th. 219, 24; Dan. 59. (c) of fire, sky :-- Reád líg, Dóm. L. 10, 149, 152 : Exon. Th. 51, 2; Cri. 810. Ðes heofon ys reád (rubicundum), Mt. Kmbl. 16, 2. (d) of blood :-- Sió reáde ród the bloodstained cross, Exon. 68, 11; Cri. 1102. [Goth. rauds : O. Sax. ród : O. Frs. rád : O. H. Ger. rót : Icel. rauðr.] v. bleó-, geolu-, weolc-reád ; reód.
reáda glosses tolia vel porunula :-- Smæle þearmas ilia, reáda tolia vel porunula, bæcþearm entales, Wrt. Voc. i. 44, 46-48.
reádan. v. on-reádan.
reád-basu; adj. Reddish purple :-- Ð&aelig-acute;r synt ða reádbeswean blóstman grówende, L. E. I. prm. ; Th. ii. 400, 5.
reádda, an; m. The robin redbreast :-- Raedda rubisca, Wrt. Voc. ii. 119. 38. Cf. rudduc.
reáde; adv. Redly, in red :-- Hire andwlita biþ reáde wan livid with a red tinge, Lchdm. ii. 348, 19. Ðá wearþ beám monig blódigum teárum birunnen reáde and þicce, Exon. Th. 72, 22; Cri. 1176. Ic eom reáde bew&aelig-acute;fed I am clothed in red, 484, 2; Rä. 70, 1.
reád-fáh; adj. Red-stained, having patches of red colour :-- Wág reádfáh, Exon. Th. 476, 19; Ruin. 10.
reádian; p. ode To be or become red :-- Ic reádige rubeo, Ælfc. Gr. 26, 2; Som. 28, 42. Reádaþ þe heofun rutilat coelum, Mt. Kmbl. Rush. 16, 3. Reádode purpurescit, Wrt. Voc. ii. 67,
8. Reádede, Hpt. Gl. 503, 51. Reádodon rubescunt, Hymn. Surt. 52, 31. Æppel ðe ðonne gyt ne reádige, Lchdm. i. 330, 22. Smire ða ófras ð&aelig-acute;r hit reádige, ii. 108, 20. Reádian rubescere, Hymn. Surt. 49, 17. Reádiendum rubente, 91, 33. [O. H. Ger. róten rutilare, rubere, erubescere.] v. reódian.
reád-leáf (?); adj. Having red leaves :-- On ða hreádleáfan &aelig-acute;c, Cod. Dip. Kmbl. v. 179, 26.
reádness, e; f. Redness :-- Reádnyss rubor, Ælfc. Gr. 9, 21; Som. 10, 28. Seó reádnes ðære rósan, Blickl. Homl. 7, 29. Seó reádnes ðæs swyles rubor tumoris, Bd. 4, 19; S. 589, 31. Reádnysse ostro, purpura, vermiculo, Hpt. Gl. 503, 49 : 522, 6.
reád-staled; adj. Having a red stale or stalk :-- Reádstalede hárhuna, Lchdm. i. 378, 19.
reád-stán (?), es; m. Ruddle, red ochre :-- Rédestán sinopide, Wrt. Voc. ii. 120, 63. [O. H. Ger. rót-stein sinopis, Grff. 6, 688.]
reáf, es; n. I. spoil, booty :-- Reáf exuviae, spolia, Wrt. Voc. ii. 146, 33 : exuvias, 31, 56 : 93, 1. Weorðlíc reáf spolia, Ps. Th. 67, 12. Se ðe beorna reáf manige (spolia multa) méteþ, 118, 162. Seó gýtsung hyre reáf (spolia) on ðære wynstran sídan scylt, Gl. Prud. 56 a. Hý ðý reáfe r&aelig-acute;dan mótan, Exon. Th. 110, 5; Gú. 103. II. raiment, a garment, robe, vestment :-- Reáf vestis vel vestimentum vel indumentum, Wrt. Voc. i. 81, 40 : cultus, 39, 70. Heó æthrán his reáfes (vestimenti) fnæd. Heó cwæþ sóðlíce : Ic beó hál gyf ic hys reáfes æthríne, Mt. Kmbl. 9, 20-21. Tó hwí sint gé ymbhýdige be reáfe ? 6, 28. Twegen weras on hwítum reáfe in veste fulgenti, Lk. Skt. 24, 4. Ne scríde nán wíf hig mid w&aelig-acute;pmannes reáfe ne w&aelig-acute;pman mid wífmannes reáfe, Deut. 22, 5. Hé scrýdde hine mid línenum reáfe cum stola byssina, Gen. 41, 42. Hláf tó etenne and reáf tó werigenne, 28, 20. Ðæt hálie reáf ðæt Aaron wereþ, Ex. 29, 29. Johannes hæfde reáf of olfenda h&aelig-acute;rum, Mt. Kmbl. 3, 4. His reáf (vestimenta) w&aelig-acute;ron swá hwíte swá snáw, 17, 2. Hí s&aelig-acute;ton on blacum reáfum weán on wénum, Cd. Th. 191, 10; Exod. 212. Ðá dyde heó of hire wydewan reáf depositis viduitatis vestibus, Gen. 38, 14. [Laym. reaf, ræf a robe : O. Sax. nód-róf rapine : O. Frs. ráf robbery, booty; also a pledge : O. Du. roof : O. H. Ger. roub spolia, praeda : Icel. val-rauf spoils taken from the slain.] v. bed-, búr-, deáþ-, gúþ-, heaðo-, here-, lenden-, síd-, wæl-reáf.
reáfere, es; m. A reaver, robber, spoiler :-- Reáfere raptor vel praedo, vel spoliator, Wrt. Voc. i. 47, 49 : raptor, 76, 8 : agressor, 19, 7. Hreáfere praedo, raptor, Hpt. Gl. 501, 34. Gif hwilc þeóf oððe reáfere gesóhte ðone cyning, ðæt hé hæbbe nigon nihta fyrst, L. Ath. iv. 4; Th. i. 222, 26. Ueriatus wæs micel þeófmon and on ðære stalunge hé wearð reáfere Viriathus latro, primum infestando vias, deinde vastando provincias, Ors. 5, 2; Swt. 216, 8. Git ðú on hwilcum men ongitst ðæt hé byþ gítsere and reáfere, ne scealt ðú hine ná hátan man, ac wulf, Bt. 37, 4; Fox 192, 15. Ne s&aelig-acute;de ðæt godspel ðæt se ríca (Dives in the parable) reáfere w&aelig-acute;re, ac wæs uncystig, Homl. Th. i. 328, 18. Scyld sceal cempan, sceaft reáfere, Exon. Th. 341, 23; Gn. Ex. 130. Ic ne eom swylce óðre men, reáferas (raptores), Lk. Skt. 18, 11. Rýperas and reáferas and ðás woruldstrúderas, L. I. P. 2; Th. ii. 304, 19 : Wulfst. 165, 35 : L. C. S. 7; Th. i. 380, 5. [O. E. Homl. reaferes, reveres; pl. : A. R. reavares : Laym. ræveres : Piers P. reveres : O. H. Ger. roubari raptor, predo : Ger. räuber : Icel. raufari, reyfari.]
